contract.settlement_definition: YES settles on the final official margin of the single named game: the named team wins outright (KXNCAAMBGAME, D3GAME, CBC, conference-tournament game series, title only), wins by more than a .5 floor_strike (KXNCAAMBSPREAD, so no push exists), wins by a stated bucket such as 6 to 10 (KXNCAAMBWINMARGIN), or satisfies a conjunction of a spread cover and a total under (KXNCAAMBSGP). The game is identified by teams and the originally scheduled date. A postponement that still tips within 48 hours stays open; cancelled or not started inside 48 hours resolves to a fair price (neither YES nor NO). The sampled full-game rules never state whether overtime is included, only that the market resolves on the official final result.

rules_evidence.quote: wins by more than 50.5 points in the Queens University vs Oklahoma St. men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread strikes are 'wins by more than X.5' on the game identified by the original scheduled date; a 50.5-point strike shows the series lists mismatch buy games with extreme margins.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start, all markets will resolve to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cancellation or a more than 48 hour delay voids the event at a fair price, so the label is censored, not NO.

rules_evidence.quote: If Michigan wins the game by 6 to 10 points in the Michigan vs UConn men's college basketball game
rules_evidence.establishes: The winning-margin series is a set of mutually exclusive margin buckets, so the whole margin distribution (not only the median) is the target.

rules_evidence.quote: collectively score under 144.5 total points in the UConn at Michigan men's college basketball game
rules_evidence.establishes: The same-game parlay is a conjunction of a spread cover and a total, so the joint distribution of margin and total, not two marginals, settles it.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: no sampled full-game rule says whether OT points count toward the margin; the 2nd-half series explicitly says including overtime, so the full-game wording relies on 'official final result' and is inferred, not verified. A five-minute OT collapses most close games to a 1-to-6 point margin.
Strikes end in .5 so there is no push; WINMARGIN buckets (for example 6 to 10) have integer edges so a margin of exactly 5 or 11 falls in a neighbour bucket.

KXNCAAMBGAME, D3GAME, CBC, HL and MARMADREGION are TITLE_ONLY: their rules text was not sampled, so tie-break, forfeit and tournament-advancement wording (a region winner is a multi-game event) is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Mismatch buy games (a 50.5-point strike against a Division I newcomer) and Division III opponents (D3GAME) have no standard rating coverage; margins there are driven by bench-clearing, not by the efficiency gap.
Postponement within 48 hours keeps the market open but moves tip time, so lineup news and rest assumptions made at open can be stale.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score as published for the game (NCAA/ESPN box score); the sampled rules cite 'the official final result' without naming a provider, so provider hierarchy on score corrections is unverified.

mechanism.summary: A college game margin is a sum of possession-level scoring differences, so the expected margin is the tempo-scaled gap between two opponent-adjusted efficiency ratings plus a venue term, and the margin sd scales with the square root of possessions (roughly 10 to 11 points for a typical game, wider when tempo is high or three-point reliance is large). The mean is poorly known: rosters turn over heavily through the transfer portal, so early-season ratings are priors with large posterior sd, and who actually plays (often undisclosed) shifts the mean by points. Around the mean the realised margin is not a clean Gaussian: favourites in lopsided games pull starters and let leads erode (compressing spread covers for big favourites), and trailing teams foul late (inflating the favourite's final margin by free throws while leaving winner probability unchanged), so winner, cover, bucket and parlay contracts read different parts of one mixture-shaped distribution.

stages.name: Latent strength gap with roster-churn prior
stages.description: Each side has a latent per-possession strength (offense minus defense, opponent-adjusted) that must be estimated from a thin schedule: about 30 games, a connected graph only through conference play, and heavy roster turnover through the transfer portal. Early in the season the preseason prior (returning minutes, portal arrivals, recruiting, coach) carries most weight; by January the in-season ratings dominate. The gap is a posterior, not a point, and its sd is largest for new-roster teams and for isolated schedules. Unrated opponents (Division III, newly reclassifying D1 schools) have no rating at all and need a tier prior.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior on the rating gap with sd shrinking roughly like 1/sqrt(games played); heavy-tailed for new rosters and for opponents with fewer than a handful of D1 games.

stages.name: Who actually plays tonight
stages.description: The strength gap is conditional on the active rotation. College programs have no mandated injury report, so a star's status is often revealed minutes before tip through starters lists or warm-up news, and the market may price the scratch before a pregame feed does. The effect of an absence depends on replacement quality and bench depth: with a seven-man rotation a missing starter costs more than in a ten-man one. The model must treat status as a probability mixture over scenarios rather than as a label.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over rotation scenarios (starter in/out, minutes-limited), each shifting the mean by roughly 0 to 6 points; probabilities of each scenario are themselves uncertain and time-dependent.

stages.name: Venue, travel and schedule-spot shift
stages.description: Home court adds a mean shift of about three to four points on average but varies by arena, crowd and altitude, and collapses toward zero or reverses on neutral floors (in-season events, conference tournaments, the Crown). Rest, travel and third-games-in-days effects are small in college but matter in multi-game events. Schedule spots (buy games, rivalry, post-exam lull, lookahead to conference play) change effort and rotation, which feeds the blowout stage as much as the mean.
stages.distribution: Approximately constant shift per venue class with team-specific deviations that need heavy shrinkage (team home edge is noisy over about 15 home games); schedule-spot effects are small and unevenly measurable.

stages.name: Possession count and margin variance
stages.description: Final margin variance is not a constant: it grows with the number of possessions and with three-point reliance (three-point shooting is a high-variance way to score). The slower side often controls tempo, so a low-possession game with an underdog that shoots many threes widens the effective upset probability beyond what the same mean gap gives in a fast game. Expected possession count is a negotiated quantity from both teams' adjusted tempo.
stages.distribution: Margin sd scales approximately with sqrt(possessions) times a shot-profile factor; tempo itself has about 3 to 4 possession residual sd; pace control is asymmetric (slow team usually wins the argument).

stages.name: Late-game script and blowout compression
stages.description: Observed margin differs from the in-game 'true' margin through two end-of-game mechanisms. In a lopsided game the favourite's coach substitutes freely, so the lead decays or stalls; whether a 25-point halftime lead ends at 18 or 30 depends heavily on the coach's bench-clearing habit and on the opponent's garbage-time scoring. In a close game the trailing team fouls and the leader's free-throw conversion extends or protects the margin without changing who wins. Overtime converts a tied game into a 1 to 6 point margin.
stages.distribution: Regime mixture: competitive regime (margin approximately normal) and blowout regime (compressed with a coach-specific decay), with overtime adding a spike of 1 to 6 point margins; the mixture weight is a threshold-like function of the expected margin.

stages.name: Contract mapping and joint outcomes
stages.description: The same margin distribution settles different contracts. Moneyline reads P(margin > 0), spread reads a tail at a .5 strike, winning margin reads a bucket pmf, and the same-game parlay needs the joint of margin and total because favourites in blowouts both cover and (through starters resting) tend to push totals under or over depending on tempo. Settlement frictions (postponement beyond 48 hours resolves to fair price, official score vs a later correction) censor or relabel rows.
stages.distribution: Discrete integer margin with a continuous latent; correlation between margin and total is weakly positive for fast favourites and negative when a blowout slows scoring; void probability is small but nonzero (a few percent in early-season weather or cancellation windows).

cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.label: Tier prior for unrated or newly reclassifying opponents
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.mechanism: Division III, NAIA and first-year D1 transition schools have no or almost no D1 games, so adjusted-efficiency ratings do not exist or are one-game noise; margin must come from a tier prior with a very wide sd.
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.rationale: The ledger lists a D3 game series and a spread strike of 50.5 against a D1 newcomer. A rating pipeline that silently fills these with the league mean gives wrong means and understated variance; the market in these games is thin and can be stale.
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.measurement: For each opponent with fewer than 8 D1 games in the current season, replace its rating with prior = tier_mean + 0.5*(conference_or_division_mean - tier_mean) learned from past seasons of the same tier (D3 vs D1 buy games, reclassifying schools in years 1 to 4), in points per 100 possessions; set prior sd to the empirical sd of that tier's rating residual (about 3 times the sd of an established D1 team). As-of: use the rating snapshot taken before tip; update with the opponent's own prior-game results with weight n/(n+8).
free_sources: Sports-Reference CBB schedule and game logs
NCAA stats site D3 and D1 records
raw_data: historical game results of D1 vs D3 and D1 vs transitioning schools with final margins
opponent D1 games played to date
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.why: Separates the genuinely extreme-margin buy games (strikes in the 40s) from ordinary games and tells the model that variance and mean uncertainty are larger and asymmetric there.

cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.label: Coach-specific bench-clearing and lead-protection behaviour
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.mechanism: How quickly a coach removes starters and what pace he plays once ahead by a lot determines how much of an in-game lead survives to the final margin.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.rationale: Cover probability at large spreads is dominated by the end-of-game margin decay, not by the pregame mean. Some coaches play starters until a 30-point lead; others empty the bench at +20 by the second-half under-12 timeout. This is a stable trait across seasons (coach, not roster), unlike team scoring luck.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: for every game in which a team led by at least 15 at any media timeout, compute lead_at_time_t (t = 12:00, 8:00, 4:00 remaining) and the final margin; coach_decay = mean(final_margin - lead_at_8min) per 8 minutes of game time, estimated over the coach's last 4 seasons with shrinkage weight n/(n+15) to the league mean decay, split by lead bucket (15 to 25, over 25). Also compute the share of second-half minutes played by the top-5 minutes players when ahead by 20 or more.
raw_data: play-by-play with game clock and score
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.why: Gives the compression term for large favourite spreads and winning-margin buckets that rating gaps cannot explain.

cbb.margin_regime_mixture.label: Competitive versus blowout regime mixture of the final margin
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.mechanism: Final margin is a mixture of a competitive regime (late fouling, overtime) and a blowout regime (compressed, coach-dependent), with the mixing weight a threshold function of the expected margin.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.rationale: A single normal with sd 10 mis-prices tails at both ends: too fat in the blowout regime for favourites covering large numbers, and too thin right at tied-game and overtime-driven 1 to 5 point margins. Winning-margin buckets and 40+ point spreads sit in exactly these regimes.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.measurement: Fit on historical closing-line-independent model expected margins m_hat: P(blowout)=logistic(a + b*|m_hat| + c*coach_decay) with a normal-in-regime margin for each regime (mu_k, sd_k) and a discrete overtime spike mass at margins 1 to 6 whose weight equals P(tie at 0:00) from the ot model; output the integer-margin pmf (for strikes at .5 and win-margin buckets) at pregame as-of; refit each season with at least 10 prior seasons.
raw_data: historical final scores with OT flag
pregame expected margin per game (model output)
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.why: Specifies the shape every contract in this archetype reads: moneyline, spread tail, win-margin bucket probabilities.

cbb.margin_total_covariance.label: Joint distribution of margin and total for same-game parlays
cbb.margin_total_covariance.mechanism: Margin and total are not independent: tempo and scoring-environment shocks move both teams' points together while blowouts reshape both margin and total through bench play and clock use.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.rationale: KXNCAAMBSGP is a conjunction of a spread cover and a total; pricing it as the product of two marginals mis-prices a systematic correlation, typically positive for favourites in fast games (favourite scores more, total higher) and negative when a slow favourite grinds.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.measurement: Estimate corr(margin_resid, total_resid) from standardized residuals (actual minus model expectation, divided by game-level sd) bucketed by favourite size (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+) and by team tempo tercile, with shrinkage to the pooled correlation weight n/(n+200) per bucket; as-of all prior games; apply through a bivariate normal copula with the regime mixture margins.
raw_data: historical final score for both teams per game
pregame expected margin and expected total from the model
cbb.margin_total_covariance.why: The only way to price the parlay legs coherently with the spread and the total contracts; absent from the existing list.

cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.label: Point-in-time rating snapshots (no retroactive revision)
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.mechanism: Free rating sites recompute the whole season after each game and revise past ratings; a rating pulled today for a past date contains information from games after that date.
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.rationale: A backtest or live feature using the current rating page overstates edge via look-ahead; archival snapshots are rare and paid for KenPom. The strength gap input is only valid if it equals the number visible before tip.
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.measurement: Store, each day by 06:00 ET, adj_off, adj_def, tempo, games_played, rank and the schedule-adjustment version for every D1 team from the chosen source; define the feature rating_gap(game) as the snapshot value from the last snapshot before tip minus the venue term; add snapshot_age_hours and an indicator for rating-method revision dates; for history use time-machine pages only where timestamps exist, otherwise rebuild from game results using a fixed algorithm.
free_sources: Bart Torvik time machine (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for full coverage)
raw_data: daily rating tables by team with timestamps
game results to rebuild ratings point-in-time
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.why: Guards the central strength input against leakage specific to how CBB ratings are published.

cbb.ratings.reason: Core strength term, but the entry says 'plus market-implied', which contaminates a fundamentals input with a benchmark; keep the free-rating ensemble only and carry the market separately.

cbb.adj_off.reason: Needed to build the tempo-scaled margin and style matchup; for a pure side contract the net rating already carries most information, so offense alone is secondary.

cbb.adj_def.reason: Same reasoning as offense; its luck regression on opponent shooting matters because defensive efficiency is the noisier half in a 30-game sample.

cbb.rating_uncertainty.reason: Posterior sd of the gap decides how wide the winner and spread distribution is early in the season and for isolated schedules; correctly primary.

cbb.preseason_prior.reason: With heavy portal turnover the prior is most of the information through roughly December; primary for early-season games, fading afterwards.

cbb.in_season_improvement.reason: Hard to separate from regular ratings drift and rotation settling, small effect sizes with high noise; keep only as a slope term inside the prior update, not a standalone feature.

cbb.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Translates availability into a mean shift; only as good as the player-impact inputs and the status probabilities beneath it.

cbb.injuries.reason: Largest controllable mean shift and also where the market may be ahead; the as-of vintage of the status matters more than the label.

cbb.status_disclosure.reason: Useful to convert vague statuses into probabilities, but the calibration sample is tiny for college; a conference-level prior is the realistic starting point.

cbb.starters.reason: Confirmed lineups arrive near tip, often after the tradable window; useful for labelling but not for early pricing.

cbb.venue.reason: Home court is the largest non-talent term; includes altitude as a sub-case.

cbb.home_court_team.reason: Team-specific home edges are noisy on a 15-game home sample; only valid with heavy shrinkage to the league mean.

cbb.neutral_site.reason: Needed for events and conference tournaments where nominal home teams get partial crowd advantage.

cbb.rest_travel.reason: Rest effect in college is small except in tournament formats; context that moderates variance rather than the mean.

cbb.motivation.reason: Stakes are real but this is a hard-to-quantify label with partial knowability; unless turned into measurable variables (seed race, bubble) it is anecdotal.

cbb.pace_mismatch.reason: Correctly a variance term: possession count controls margin sd, so mismatches in pace change cover probabilities for the underdog.

cbb.three_pt_dist.reason: Volatility term for the underdog; needs the three-point attempt share and luck-adjusted rates to avoid double counting with the rating ensemble.

cbb.score_resid.reason: Shape of residuals is needed, but it must be a model residual and not a residual against a market line (which would be a benchmark).

cbb.size_rebounding.reason: Mismatch effects are largely already inside efficiency; useful only for interaction with pace and zone.

cbb.defense_style.reason: Style effects on margin are small relative to rating error; keep for matchup variance (press and zone produce turnover-driven swings).

m.quote_history.reason: Price path shows what is already priced; it is a timing diagnostic, not an outcome driver, and must not enter the outcome model.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the settled event (strike, bucket, void window); the contract input that decides labels.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook closing and opening numbers are the comparison prior; using them as a model input removes the ability to measure edge.

m.ladder_structure.reason: A cross-rung consistency check on market prices, valuable for coherence between spread, win-margin and moneyline quotes but derived from the market.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Execution capacity, not outcome information; matters for sizing, not for probability.

cbb.market_calibration_bias.reason: Describes the market's reliability by price bucket; a post-model shading term and not an input to margin probability.

m.volume_oi.reason: Liquidity of a game says nothing about the margin; at most a scaling for sizing.

m.trade_tape.reason: Informed-flow hypothesis based on prints; market-derived and untested, so not an outcome input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Defines labels and timing but is not a predictor; the correct provider and correction handling must be pinned.

cbb.lineups.reason: Lineup on/off data validate availability adjustments, but five-man sample sizes are small; use at the player level with shrinkage.

cbb.player_impact.reason: Value-over-replacement of each rotation player converts absences into points; provider differences (BPM vs EvanMiya) are material.

cbb.roster_minutes.reason: Bench depth moderates the absence effect; it is an input to the lineup-adjusted rating rather than a separate predictor.

m.lifecycle.reason: Defines the tradable information set (close time vs last lineup news) for evaluation; not a predictor.

interactions.mechanism: The same rating gap converts into a larger expected margin in a high-possession game and a smaller one in a low-possession game, so the spread is gap times possession ratio, and the underdog's cover chance is higher in slow games where margin sd is also smaller relative to the number.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised margin on gap, possessions and gap x possessions using prior-season games; check whether residual sd falls with sqrt(possessions) and whether the gap coefficient scales with tempo.

interactions.mechanism: Once the expected margin passes roughly 15 to 20 points the game flips into a blowout regime whose end-of-game compression depends on the coach: a lead-protecting coach turns a model margin of 25 into a 14 point cover miss, while a starter-heavy coach does not. Below the threshold the coach term is irrelevant.
interactions.how_to_test: Split games by predicted margin bucket and compare final-margin minus lead-at-8-minutes across coaches with high and low decay; verify the difference vanishes below 12 points.

interactions.mechanism: Early in the season (before about 8 games) the prior carries the weight and uncertainty is highest, so the weight on the in-season improvement slope should be near zero; by February the same slope is a useful signal. The correct blend depends on games played and on roster continuity.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare out-of-sample margin error of the gap using prior-only, ratings-only and blended versions in game-number buckets (0-5, 6-12, 13-20, 21+) and test for a crossing point.

interactions.mechanism: A starter's absence costs more points for a team with a short rotation and a low-quality replacement than for a deep team; the effect is also larger when the missing player controls the ball, since the replacement changes turnovers and pace as well as scoring.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with known absences, regress margin shift on player impact value interacted with bench-depth index and replacement impact; compare to a flat per-player shift.

interactions.mechanism: Home advantage is a three-regime piecewise term: full home court, neutral floor, and semi-home (conference tournaments held in a nearby arena); the team-specific deviation applies to the full-home regime and shrinks toward zero otherwise.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate venue coefficients by regime from historical margins and test whether team-specific home edges survive out of sample only in the home regime.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped probit link from rating gap to win probability; fat tails in lopsided matchups
nonlinearities.why: A 20-point expected margin is not a 99.9 percent win in practice because rating error, an injury scenario or a cold-shooting night keep upset mass near 1 to 4 percent; with a normal link the tail is understated.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 to 20 expected margin points above which lead decay appears
nonlinearities.why: Cover probabilities for big favourites fall sharply once the game is expected to be non-competitive because coaches clear benches; below the threshold the effect is zero, which is why a linear term fails.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating decay with games played (approximately 1/sqrt(n)), floor from roster change
nonlinearities.why: Posterior sd falls fast over the first 8 to 10 games and slowly afterwards, with a floor because injuries and rotation changes keep re-introducing uncertainty; treating it as constant overstates early certainty.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAMBTOTAL settles YES when the combined points of both teams in the named game exceed the half-point floor_strike (strike_type greater, so no push). KXNCAAMBOT is a different discrete event on the same game: YES when at least N overtime periods are played (floor_strike 2.5 for the sampled '3+ overtime periods' contract). The game is identified by teams and original scheduled date; a postponement that tips within 48 hours stays open and resolves on the official final result, and a cancelled or later-than-48-hour game resolves to a fair price. The rules do not say that overtime points are included in the total, only that it resolves on the official final result.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 126.5 total points are scored in the Middle Tennessee vs Kansas men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The total is one-sided over a .5 strike on both teams' points in the game, identified by original scheduled date.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 3 overtime periods are played in the Valparaiso vs Purdue men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The overtime series is a count-of-extra-periods event (here 3 or more), a very rare tail separate from the points total.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: A short postponement does not void the market; the settlement source is the official final result.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion in the points total is not spelled out in the sampled TOTAL rules (compare 2H markets which explicitly say inclusive of overtime); the total strike therefore has an unverified OT component worth roughly 10 to 12 points in the 5 to 6 percent of games that go to extra time.
KXNCAAMBOT is a count contract: strike 2.5 for 3+ periods, so lower strikes (1+, 2+) are presumably separate rungs; only the 3+ rung's text was sampled.
Strikes ending in .5 mean no push; adjacent rungs of the same game (for example 126.5 and 127.5) are nested events with a monotone probability curve.
A game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than NO, so early-season weather or arena issues create censored labels.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game as stated in the rules ('official final result'); no named provider (NCAA, ESPN or school sites) in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: Total points are possessions times combined points per possession plus an overtime tail. Possessions come from a negotiation of two adjusted tempos moderated by average possession length, shot-clock violations and turnover or foul stoppages; per-possession scoring comes from opponent-adjusted offense versus defense, shot profile (three-point share and rim rate) and free-throw production, with a large luck component in shooting that mean-reverts. The result is a roughly normal distribution with an sd near 11 to 12 points, plus a right tail created by overtime (about 5 to 6 percent of games, adding about 10 to 12 points) and late-game intentional fouling in close games, and a left tail created by blowouts with bench play and by teams that slow a game when ahead. Availability changes tempo as well as efficiency (a missing lead guard usually lowers possessions), and the league-wide scoring baseline drifts across a season and across rule-emphasis years.

stages.name: Possession count from two tempos
stages.description: Expected possessions are not the average of two adjusted tempos: each side's average possession length, its transition share and how long it works the shot clock decide how much of the 40 minutes becomes possessions, and the defence that forces long possessions stretches the count. Turnover rate and the number of whistles (each foul stops the clock and ends a possession) subtract or add possessions. The slower team usually controls the pace, so an interaction of the two tempos is needed rather than a mean.
stages.distribution: Possession count approximately normal around 65 to 72 with a game-level sd near 3 to 4; the pace-control asymmetry skews the realised count toward the slower team's preference.

stages.name: Points per possession from two adjusted units
stages.description: Each team's expected points per possession is its opponent-adjusted offence against the other side's adjusted defence, modified by shot profile (rim, mid-range, three share) and the four factors (shooting, turnovers, offensive rebounding, free throws). A large share of recent shooting results is luck: three-point and free-throw percentages regress hard to shot quality and to talent, particularly for teams with a high three-point attempt share. League-wide scoring level also drifts through the season and with rule emphasis, so the baseline must move with a short half-life.
stages.distribution: Per-possession points approximately normal with a game-level sd that depends on shot mix; three-point-heavy games have visibly wider sd than rim-and-free-throw games.

stages.name: Whistle and free-throw production
stages.description: Foul and free-throw volume is set by the crew's calls per game, the teams' foul-drawing and foul-committing rates, and the bonus structure (1-and-1 at the 7th team foul in a half, two shots from the 10th). Free throws are points without clock time, so a high-foul game both lengthens the game and lifts efficiency, in proportion to the teams' free-throw percentage. The crew is often assigned late and unannounced, which limits how much can be used pregame.
stages.distribution: Free-throw attempts per game are overdispersed (sd about 6 to 7 around a mean near 35 combined), and the crew effect is a few points of total per game at most.

stages.name: Personnel and rotation effects on both inputs
stages.description: A missing creator reduces possessions and transition scoring at the same time and usually costs the offence more than the defence; a missing rim protector raises opponent efficiency without affecting tempo. Because injury news in college is thin, the realised lineup is a mixture and the total's mean inherits that mixture. Rest and travel add small fatigue effects mainly in multi-game events.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over scenarios (key creator or rim protector in or out) with combined mean shifts of about 1 to 5 points of total.

stages.name: Late-game script and overtime tail
stages.description: Close games end with deliberate fouling by the trailing team, which converts each remaining possession into one or two free throws and adds points, while a blowout reduces efficiency through bench units and often shortens possessions. A tie at the end of regulation adds five minutes of extra play, about 10 to 12 combined points in the sampled game and rarely a second or third extra period. These two end-of-game mechanisms create a right tail and a left tail that a symmetric distribution around the mean misses.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed mixture: normal body, overtime spike (+10 to +12) with probability near 5 to 6 percent, and a late-fouling add of a few points concentrated in games within five points at the two-minute mark.

stages.name: Contract mapping: total strikes versus overtime count
stages.description: The over strike reads the upper tail of one distribution, and adjacent rungs are nested events whose probabilities must fall monotonically with the strike. The overtime-count contract reads an entirely different object: the probability the game is tied at 40:00 and then tied again after each extra period, which is a few tenths of a percent for three or more extra periods. Settlement frictions (OT inclusion in the points total not stated, void windows) change the label.
stages.distribution: Total: integer points with a smooth tail; OT count: geometric-like chain with a per-period tie probability in the low tens of percent, so 3+ periods is of order one in a thousand games.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted offence and defence form the per-possession scoring baseline for both teams; no player-level talent term beyond lineups.

opponent_matchup.note: Interaction of one side's shot profile with the other's defence matters for totals; shot-zone data exists in the catalog but was not attached to this archetype.

role_personnel.note: Who handles the ball changes tempo; who protects the rim changes opponent efficiency.

availability_news.note: Pregame availability probabilities; thin disclosure in college is the limitation and is listed as unresolved.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching scheme appears through tempo choices and possession length; no explicit coach-level variable beyond that.

environment.note: Altitude and arena effects plus a slowly drifting league baseline by month and rule emphasis.

game_context_script.note: Late-fouling points and overtime are explicit tail mechanisms.

pace_volume.note: Possession count from average possession length rather than a single tempo number.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck versus skill split for three-point and free-throw conversion is central because the sample is about 30 games.

distribution_variance.note: Game-level sd depends on tempo and three-point share; right skew from overtime.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Small fatigue effect; mostly relevant in multi-game events where totals may drop.

officiating_rules.note: Crew whistle tendency feeds free-throw volume; crews are announced late for most games.

settlement_contract.note: Strike (.5, no push), OT count contract, void rule; OT inclusion in points is not verified.

cbb.possession_length_profile.label: Average possession length and transition share (offence and defence)
cbb.possession_length_profile.mechanism: Possessions in 40 minutes equal 2400 seconds divided by average possession length plus dead time; a team's offence length and its defence-forced length both matter.
cbb.possession_length_profile.rationale: A single adjusted tempo hides the matchup: a team that attacks early facing a defence that forces shot-clock-long possessions plays slower than the average of tempos suggests; this is the first-order total driver, since a three-possession error is about three to four points of total.
cbb.possession_length_profile.measurement: For team A vs B: APL_game = 0.5*(APL_off_A + APL_def_B) and 0.5*(APL_off_B + APL_def_A) in seconds from the season to date with half-life 6 weeks and shrinkage n/(n+10) to the league mean; expected possessions = 2400 / mean(APL_game) - dead_time adjustment (about 0.4 possessions per 5 team fouls above the mean); calibrate to realised possessions (FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TO) on prior-season games, output possessions and an sd. As-of: stats published before tip.
raw_data: team season-to-date average possession length offence and defence
cbb.possession_length_profile.why: Totals depend on the matchup's pace, not either team's average; the existing tempo input collapses this.

cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.label: Overtime reach and repeat-tie chain
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.mechanism: P(OT) is the probability of a tie at the end of regulation (a function of expected margin, total and variance); each additional period needs another tie, with per-period tie probability set by five-minute scoring variance and fouling.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.rationale: KXNCAAMBOT prices counts like 3+ periods, which need P(OT) times two repeat ties, a probability of order 0.1 percent that no ordinary total or margin model produces correctly. The same chain defines the right-tail mass of the points total.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.measurement: P_tie_reg = integer pmf at margin 0 from the game's margin distribution (normal with sd = sqrt(poss/68)*10.5, centred at the model expected margin, with a discrete correction for the fact that tied scores cluster at lower margins); P_tie_OT = empirical rate of tied-after-OT among all OT periods over the last 10 seasons (per period, shrunk by count), with a multiplier for two-team free-throw rate; P(N+ periods) = P_tie_reg * P_tie_OT^(N-1); extra points per OT period = empirical mean (about 10 to 12 combined) with sd. As-of: pregame expected margin and total.
free_sources: Sports-Reference box scores with OT flag
raw_data: historical final scores with number of OT periods
points scored in each OT period (line score)
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.why: Both the OT-count contract and the right tail of the points total depend on it; the existing ot_model entry carries only a single OT probability.

cbb.total_variance_by_style.label: Game-level total variance by tempo and shot mix
cbb.total_variance_by_style.mechanism: Residual sd of the total grows with the number of possessions and with each team's three-point attempt share, as scoring becomes more lumpy.
cbb.total_variance_by_style.rationale: Rungs near the mean are insensitive to the mean error but sensitive to sd; asymmetry in tails (fat-right from OT) means a single sd mis-prices both the over and the under side of high and low strikes.
cbb.total_variance_by_style.measurement: Fit log(var(total - expected_total)) = a + b*log(expected_poss) + c*(3PA_share_A + 3PA_share_B) + d*(FTr sum) on at least 5 seasons, with expected_total taken from the model not the market; output sd per game, and a skew parameter for the right tail (OT-conditioned). As-of: stats available pregame; refit annually.
cbb.total_variance_by_style.why: Specifies the width of the distribution that every total rung reads; the existing score_resid input does not condition on style.

cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.label: League-wide scoring baseline and rule-emphasis drift
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.mechanism: The national points-per-100 baseline changes by month (non-conference to conference play) and across seasons with rule emphasis, shot clock and officiating mandates.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.rationale: Adjusted ratings are relative to an average opponent; absolute totals depend on the current league mean, which moves several points per game between November and March and between rule years, and shifts early before ratings catch up.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.measurement: league_ppp_t = EWMA over the last 14 days of league-wide points per 100 possessions across all D1 games with half-life 21 days, plus an indicator for a rule-emphasis change flagged by NCAA rules committee announcements; expected total = sum of team unit ratings (relative) + 2 * league_ppp_t * expected_poss / 100; stored with timestamp so it uses only games completed before tip.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.why: Keeps the absolute level of the total anchored when ratings (relative) say nothing about the national scoring trend.

cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.label: With and without primary ball handler: pace and efficiency shift
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.mechanism: A team's possessions per 40 and transition share change when its lead guard is off the floor, and its offensive efficiency changes more than defence.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.rationale: Existing lineup inputs are labelled context and generic; the total contract needs the concrete delta in possessions and points per possession for the ball-handler absence scenario, weighted by the probability of that scenario.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.measurement: For each team's top two ball handlers (highest assist-rate plus usage), estimate delta_poss = poss_per_40_off - poss_per_40_on and delta_ppp from on/off lineup splits over the last two seasons with ridge shrinkage lambda equal to 300 possessions off-court; scenario-weighted total shift = sum_k P(absent_k) * (delta_poss_k * ppp + poss * delta_ppp_k); as-of: lineup data through the previous game.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player on/off (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for lineup splits)
raw_data: lineup on/off possession and scoring splits by player
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.why: Translates the injury mixture into total points through the pace channel specific to totals.

cbb.pace_mismatch.reason: Labelled distribution, but for totals it is a possession-count (mean) input as well as a variance one; the slow side usually wins pace control.

cbb.adj_off.reason: Opponent-adjusted offence is half of the per-possession scoring baseline; correct primary.

cbb.adj_def.reason: Other half of the scoring baseline; needs luck regression on opponent shooting.

cbb.four_factors.reason: Four-factor components are the decomposition of the same adjusted offence and defence; useful for matchups but adds no independent level information.

cbb.three_pt_luck.reason: Three-point percentage regression is the largest single source of totals error; kept secondary because its size depends on the 3PA share.

cbb.three_pt_dist.reason: Three-point reliance sets the sd and fat tails of the total rather than the mean.

cbb.free_throw.reason: FT rate times FT% determines clock-free points, with the late-game component overlapping the foul-script input.

cbb.fouls_officials.reason: Conference-level whistle tendency is a stable prior for foul volume; weak at the game level.

cbb.officials_crew.reason: The catalog entry for fouls_officials already contains the crew; the crew-specific version only differs by timing (assignments are usually known late) and should be a sub-field.

cbb.late_game_foul_script.reason: Mislabelled context: fouling points concentrate in close games and add a few points of total, so it is a secondary input with a closeness interaction.

cbb.injuries.reason: Availability changes tempo and efficiency; primary as long as it is stored as a scenario mixture with timestamps.

cbb.venue.reason: Altitude and arena effects on scoring are small outside a few venues; keep as context with venue-level fixed effects.

cbb.rest_travel.reason: College rest effects on totals are small and noisy; support exists mainly for multi-game events, so keep as a minor term only.

cbb.ot_model.reason: Needed for the tail, but a single P(OT) cannot price the 3+ period contract; extended by the OT tie chain input.

cbb.score_resid.reason: Total residual shape is the target distribution for all rungs; must be a residual from the model, not from a closing line.

m.quote_history.reason: Shows what the market already priced (for example after a lineup posting); a diagnostic, not a driver of the total.

m.rules_text.reason: Strike construction, OT-count wording and void window directly define labels for TOTAL and OT contracts.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook totals are the comparison prior; including them as input would erase measurable edge and encode their own errors.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Rung monotonicity of quoted prices is a market-derived check on a nested ladder; the model's own ladder should be monotone by construction.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Execution sizing, no information about the scoring process.

cbb.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket calibration of the market is a shading step after the model, not an input to the total distribution.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Defines the label and its timing (score corrections); not predictive.

cbb.lineups.reason: Upgrade from context: lineup pace and efficiency splits are the only way to estimate how an absence changes tempo for the total.

cbb.player_impact.reason: Quantifies how much a missing scorer shifts efficiency, but lacks a pace component; use together with the handler pace-shift input.

interactions.mechanism: A strong half-court defence that forces long possessions lowers both the number of possessions and points per possession, so the effect on the total is the product of the two reductions, larger than the sum of separate tempo and defence effects, in slow-tempo teams in particular.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total residual on tempo, adjusted defence and their product using prior seasons; check whether the interaction coefficient is negative for slow-and-strong-defence matchups.

interactions.mechanism: Recent shooting above expectation is regressed toward shot-quality expectation with weight depending on the attempt share: a team with 45 percent of shots from three has far more luck-driven variance, so its recent over-performance should be discounted harder than a rim-based team's.
interactions.how_to_test: Split teams by 3PA share and compare how well last-8-games 3P% minus season mean predicts the next game's offensive efficiency, expecting a higher regression slope for high-share teams.

interactions.mechanism: Extra fouls add points only through free-throw conversion, so the whistle effect on the total is foul count times combined free-throw percentage; a whistle-heavy crew with two poor free-throw teams adds much less than the same crew with two 78 percent teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute predicted FT points = expected FTA (crew and teams) x team FT% and test its incremental coefficient in a total residual regression versus separate linear terms.

interactions.mechanism: Intentional fouling adds points only if the game is within roughly 8 points with under two minutes left, so the add-on is a step function of projected closeness; in games decided earlier it contributes nothing and the bench-clearing effect pushes the total down.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by absolute margin at the 2:00 mark and compare points scored in the last two minutes; confirm the jump happens inside the 8-point band.

interactions.mechanism: The pace effect of an injury exists only if the missing player is one of the team's primary ball handlers, and its sign differs from a rim-protector absence, so the injury input must be mapped to a role before it can shift the total.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with a missing starter, compare changes in possessions per 40 by player role (handler vs big) against the team's season average.

nonlinearities.shape: step addition of 10 to 12 combined points with probability 5 to 6 percent; right skew
nonlinearities.why: Overtime is a mixture component: it shifts the upper tail of the total by a block of points rather than adding a small smooth amount, which matters for high strikes where the OT bump can flip the result.

nonlinearities.shape: approximately linear in possessions but convex in the combined slow-slow region because shot-clock violations and long possessions hold scoring down
nonlinearities.why: When both teams are in the slowest tail of tempo, each possession tends to end later in the shot clock, lowering per-possession efficiency, so total falls faster than a linear mapping from possessions suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: variance of total increases convexly with combined three-point attempt share
nonlinearities.why: Each additional three-point attempt replaces a lower-variance two or free-throw attempt, so total sd grows faster than the mean when both teams shoot many threes, shifting probability into both tails of the strike ladder.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAMBTEAMTOTAL settles YES when the named team's own points in the identified game exceed the .5 floor_strike (strike_type greater, so no push). It is a one-team slice of the final score, tied to the game by teams and original scheduled date. A game that is postponed but tips within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price. The sampled text does not say whether overtime points count toward the team's score; it names the official final result only. The rung ladder per game is a nested set of strikes whose probabilities must be monotone in the strike.

rules_evidence.quote: If Michigan scores more than 89.5 points in the Michigan vs UConn men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Settles on one named team's own points over a .5 strike, in a game identified by its original date.

rules_evidence.quote: all markets will resolve to a fair price
rules_evidence.establishes: Cancellation or a delay beyond 48 hours voids the event at a fair price instead of resolving NO.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion in a team's points is not stated in the sampled rules; the official final score would include it, adding about 5 to 6 points to each team in the roughly 5 to 6 percent of games that go to extra time.
The sampled strike (89.5 for a team in a game with a presumably high total) shows team-total rungs sit well above typical team scores, so the market spans a wide tail rather than only the median.

Only one series (KXNCAAMBTEAMTOTAL) exists; the home and away team each have their own ladder in the same game and the two ladders are positively correlated through pace and negatively through blowout shape.
Neutral-site or tournament games name teams by listing order, so the home/away label cannot be relied on to identify the venue effect.

mechanism.summary: One team's points are the game's possession count (shared with the opponent, so differing by at most one) times that team's points per possession, plus overtime points. The possession count is a negotiation of both tempos, but the team's own scoring rate depends on its offence versus the opponent's defence, its shot profile against that defence's scheme (zone, press, rim protection), free-throw production against the opponent's foul propensity, and the shooting luck component that regresses. Unlike the game total, a team total is coupled to the margin: a favourite's points saturate once its starters sit in a blowout and the opponent's bench and late-fouling free throws then decide how many points the underdog gets, so one team's distribution is shifted and skewed by its role in the game script.

stages.name: Shared possession count and team pace control
stages.description: Both teams have almost exactly the same number of possessions, so a team cannot buy extra scoring chances alone; its own points depend on the game's tempo, which is set by whichever team imposes its preferred pace. Some teams are elastic (they speed up against a fast opponent), others dictate regardless; this elasticity matters because a pace-setting team facing a slower opponent gets fewer possessions than its adjusted tempo implies, and the market may assume the average of tempos.
stages.distribution: Possessions approximately normal with sd 3 to 4, shared by both teams; team-specific elasticity to opponent pace ranges from near zero (pace dictators) to near one (pace adapters).

stages.name: Own points per possession against this defence
stages.description: A team's expected points per possession is its adjusted offence against the specific defence it faces, adjusted for shot profile (a rim-attacking team against a shot-blocking centre, a three-point-heavy team against a zone that gives threes), turnover pressure from presses, and the four factors. Scoring luck is large in a 30-game sample, so recent three-point hot streaks are regressed toward shot-quality expectation, with the regression stronger for teams that shoot many threes.
stages.distribution: Per-possession scoring approximately normal for one team with game-level sd about 8 to 9 points of team total from shooting variance, and a mean that depends on the scheme interaction.

stages.name: Free-throw production against the foul profile
stages.description: Free throws are points that cost no clock. How many a team gets depends on how it attacks (rim and post trips draw fouls) and on how many fouls the opponent commits per possession; the bonus rules (1-and-1 at the 7th team foul in a half, two shots from the 10th) raise the yield of every late-half foul. Conversion depends on the team's free-throw percentage with a regression toward talent in small samples.
stages.distribution: Free-throw attempts for one team are overdispersed (sd about 5 around a mean near 18 to 20), and FT% for one game has an sd near 10 percentage points.

stages.name: Scoring role in the game script (favourite versus underdog)
stages.description: A team total is coupled to the margin in an asymmetric way. A heavy favourite scores above its base until the lead is large, then its starters sit and its per-possession scoring and pace fall, capping its total; an underdog's total is lifted by its own pace but is shaped by garbage-time bench play and late fouling free throws when trailing. The bench unit's efficiency, rather than the starters', governs how many points a team scores in the final minutes of a lopsided game.
stages.distribution: Role-dependent skew: favourite's team total is capped (left-skewed beyond a lead threshold), underdog's is right-skewed through late free throws; the coupling slope to margin is near 0.5 in the competitive zone and falls toward 0.2 in blowouts.

stages.name: Availability of own scorers and opposing defenders
stages.description: Because the contract reads one team's points, the injury effect is directional: a scorer missing for the named team lowers its total, while a missing rim protector on the opponent raises it. Disclosure is thin in college, so the mean is a mixture over scenarios. Replacement quality and the usage redistribution to remaining players determine the net loss, since part of a missing scorer's shots go to teammates at lower efficiency.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over own-scorer and opponent-defender scenarios, shifting the team total by roughly 2 to 6 points when a lead scorer is out.

stages.name: Overtime and contract mapping
stages.description: An overtime period adds roughly 5 to 6 points to each team's score, so the ladder's upper rungs include an OT mixture component. Adjacent rungs of one team's ladder are nested, and the two teams' ladders in the same game are jointly constrained by the game total and spread (home plus away points equals the total), so a consistent set of team totals needs a joint model, not two independent ones.
stages.distribution: Mixture with a small overtime component (5 to 6 percent of games, +5 to +6 points) and strong dependence between the two sides' scores through the shared possession count.

opponent_matchup.note: Zone, press and rim protection change the named team's shot mix and free-throw rate.

role_personnel.note: Who is on the floor in the final minutes of a lopsided game and who is missing among scorers.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaches differ in whether they accept the opponent's pace and in lead-protection; bench clearing is a coach-specific habit.

pace_volume.note: The count is shared between teams; own tempo alone mislabels the driver.

efficiency_conversion.note: Own shooting luck versus talent, with the opponent's three-point luck regressed too.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and travel move both teams' efficiency by a fraction of a point per 100 possessions, far below the 8 to 9 point sd of one team's score, and no stable team-specific effect has been shown in college data.

cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.label: Team pace elasticity to opponent tempo
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.mechanism: A team's realised possessions respond to opponent tempo with a team-specific slope: dictators hold their own pace, adapters match the opponent.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.rationale: The shared possession count is where own-team scoring volume comes from. Using the average of two tempos assumes a common 0.5 weight, which is wrong for many pairs and shifts a team's expected total by 2 to 4 points.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.measurement: For each team over the last two seasons regress game possessions on own adjusted tempo and opponent adjusted tempo (opponent-adjusted, centred on league mean): poss = a + b_own*(T_own - T_lg) + b_opp*(T_opp - T_lg); estimate b_own and b_opp per team with ridge shrinkage toward league coefficients (lambda equivalent to 12 games); expected game possessions for a matchup = league mean + b_own_A*(T_A - lg) + b_opp_A*(T_B - lg), averaged with the same computed from team B's coefficients, weights proportional to inverse variance. As-of: games completed before the prior day.
raw_data: both teams' season-to-date adjusted tempo before each game
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.why: Allocates the shared possession count between two teams' preferences, which is what makes a team total different from a game total.

cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.label: Coupling of one team's points to the game margin by role and spread bucket
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.mechanism: Given the total, a team's points equal (total plus margin)/2, so own points covary with margin; the covariance is not constant because blowouts reduce the total and cap the favourite's scoring.
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.rationale: A team total must be priced from the joint distribution of margin and total; treating team total as independent of the favourite or underdog role misstates skew and tails, and the coupling differs between favourites, underdogs and spread buckets.
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.measurement: Estimate k = cov(points_A, margin_A)/var(margin_A) in standardized residual form by role (favourite, underdog) and expected-margin bucket (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+) using at least 8 seasons of games with the model's own expected margins (not market lines); shrink k toward the pooled bucket value with weight n/(n+250); simulate own points as 0.5*(T + M) with T and M from the regime mixture and covariance, then take quantiles at the strike.
raw_data: historical points for and against by team
pre-game model expected margin and total
favourite/underdog flag from model not market
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.why: Gives the role-specific skew of a single team's points that a symmetric normal around the average cannot.

cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.label: Bench-unit and garbage-time-unit offensive efficiency
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.mechanism: Points per possession of units outside the top rotation (minutes below the top-6) is lower than the starters', and determines the favourite's scoring after starters sit.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.rationale: In lopsided games the final 8 to 10 minutes are played by non-starters; team total at a high strike for a favourite depends on the efficiency of those units, which differs widely between deep programmes and thin ones.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.measurement: From lineup data compute points per 100 possessions for lineups with at most 2 of the top-6 minutes players, over the last two seasons, shrunk to the team's starters-unit rating with weight n/(n+400 possessions) and to a league bench mean; stored with the share of team minutes played by such units when the team led by 15 or more (blowout minutes share). As-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player and lineup tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.why: Needed for the favourite's capped upper tail and the underdog's garbage-time points; existing inputs treat bench play only as a probability of blowout.

cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.label: Opponent foul propensity converted to the team's expected free-throw points
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.mechanism: The number of free throws the named team gets equals its drawing rate scaled by the opponent's fouls per possession and by bonus situations.
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.rationale: Free-throw points are a high-leverage part of a team total because they cost no clock; the opponent's foul rate is a stable team trait (pressure man defence or hand-checking) that the existing free-throw input measures only for the named team.
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.measurement: expected_FTA_team = poss * [0.5*FTr_team_off + 0.5*FTr_opp_def_allowed] adjusted to league mean, where FTr = FTA per 100 possessions and both terms are opponent-adjusted over the last 20 games (half-life 8 games) with shrinkage n/(n+10); expected FT points = expected_FTA * shrunk FT% * 1; as-of: games completed before tip, crew effect added as +/- 0.6 FTA per crew standard deviation when assigned.
free_sources: Bart Torvik four-factor tables (FT rate offence and defence)
raw_data: team FTA, FGA, possessions by game
officials crew for the game (if known)
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.why: Gives a matchup-specific free-throw estimate for one team's points, rather than relying on a team-level rate.

cbb.adj_def.reason: Opponent defence is the other half of the per-possession expectation; correct primary.

cbb.tempo.reason: The entry says 'own possessions' which is wrong: possessions are shared between the two teams, so the driver is game pace and pace control, not own tempo.

cbb.implied_team_totals.reason: Computed from the market spread and total; this is a benchmark prior mislabelled as primary and would remove the ability to measure deviations.

cbb.four_factors.reason: Decomposition of own offence against the opponent's four-factor defence, useful for matchup deviations; adds little on level.

cbb.shot_zones.reason: Shot mix against a rim-protecting or zone defence changes expected points per shot; limited by public data granularity.

cbb.defense_style.reason: Zone and press change both volume of threes and turnovers, which move the named team's score; strongly team specific.

cbb.three_pt_luck.reason: Three-point luck regression is the principal source of recent-form error in team scoring.

cbb.injuries.reason: Directional by team and replacement quality; one of the largest single mean shifts.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: Caps the favourite's total and shapes the underdog's; the main source of role-asymmetric skew in this archetype.

cbb.free_throw.reason: FT rate and percentage for the team; needs the opponent's foul propensity to be a matchup input.

interactions.mechanism: In competitive games a team's points rise roughly half-for-half with the margin, but once the expected margin passes about 15 the favourite's points stop rising (starters sit, possessions shorten) while the underdog's points are propped up by late fouls, so the slope flips between regimes.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the slope of points on margin separately for expected-margin buckets and favourite/underdog roles; test for a slope break near 15 points.

interactions.mechanism: A three-point-reliant offence loses efficiency against a pack-line or rim-focused man defence but gains against a zone that concedes threes; the team's baseline offence is therefore conditional on the opposing scheme, and the sign of the style effect flips with the team's shot profile.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points per possession on offence rating, opponent scheme dummy and the team's three-point share times the scheme dummy using games in which the opponent's scheme is recorded.

interactions.mechanism: When a slow-tempo team meets a fast team, whose pace wins depends on each team's elasticity: scoring volume equals the elasticity-weighted tempo times points per possession, so a team that dictates pace adds or removes points for the opponent too.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted possessions from average of tempos versus elasticity-weighted tempos against realised possessions in games with extreme tempo gaps.

interactions.mechanism: The favourite's total beyond the starters' minutes is the product of the probability of a blowout and the bench unit's scoring rate in that scenario; both are uncertain and positively linked to coach style, so they should be modelled jointly instead of averaged.
interactions.how_to_test: Use games with leads of 15 plus; compute points per possession of non-starters by coach and test if blowout probability and bench efficiency covary across teams.

interactions.mechanism: A team's free-throw points are its drawing rate times the opponent's foul propensity times conversion; a rim-attacking team against a foul-prone defence has a larger amplification than either factor suggests alone, in close games late in the half when the bonus applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team FTA on own FT rate, opponent allowed FT rate and their product, and compare to an additive specification.

nonlinearities.shape: concave saturation of the favourite's points in expected margin, with a flat segment beyond a lead of about 20
nonlinearities.why: As the favourite's lead grows, starters sit and the clock matters less, so team points stop growing and then fall relative to a linear projection; this makes high team-total strikes for big favourites systematically less likely than a total-less-spread split implies.

nonlinearities.shape: regression weight increasing in three-point attempt share and decreasing in games played (hyperbolic shrinkage)
nonlinearities.why: Shooting luck in a team total has an sd of roughly 8 to 9 points; the right amount of regression depends on how many three-point attempts underpin the observed percentage, a non-linear shrinkage rather than a fixed rate.

nonlinearities.shape: convex penalty to the opponent's scoring against elite rim protection and to the named team's three-point rate
nonlinearities.why: The effect of a very strong defence on one team's points is larger than linear because elite defences remove the highest-value shots (rim and open threes) and force low-value late-clock shots.

contract.settlement_definition: Six half-level series on one game. KXNCAAMB1H is a three-way winner market in which each team and a 'Tie in the 1st half' contract are separate YES events; KXNCAAMB1HSPREAD and KXNCAAMB1HTOTAL are .5 strikes on the first-half margin and combined first-half points. KXNCAAMB2H, 2HSPREAD and 2HTOTAL read only second-half points and explicitly include overtime. Only points scored in the named half count. The first-half events are fully settled at the break, so these markets are tradable live through the first half and, for the 2H series, up to and through halftime.

rules_evidence.quote: If neither team wins the 1st half of the Houston vs California men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 8, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The first-half winner event includes a separate tie outcome, so the three outcomes (home, away, tie) must sum to one and the tie needs its own probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 1st half count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: The period is the first half only, no overtime, independent of what happens after halftime.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: The second-half markets contain overtime points, unlike the first-half ones, so the second-half margin includes a five-minute extra-period mixture.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the 1st half by more than 8.5 points
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half spread strikes are 'wins the 1st half by more than X.5' so the half margin distribution (not the final margin) is the object.

variants_and_edge_cases: The 1H winner market has a TIE contract (YES if neither team leads at the half): probability is the integer pmf of the half margin at zero, about 4 to 6 percent for a 20-minute half, a discrete mass a normal approximation handles poorly.
2nd-half series include overtime, so the 2H margin and total contain a five-minute mixture component in the roughly 5 to 6 percent of games that go to extra time; 1st-half series never do.

The sampled secondary text for 1H, 1H spread, 1H total and 2H markets does not include the 48-hour postponement clause that the full-game series carry; postponed or delayed games at the half are therefore CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Strikes in the sample (1H total 89.5 and 2H total 87.5) are far above a typical combined 20-minute half of about 65 to 72 points, so the live ladders include extreme tail rungs; the sample strike is not an estimate of the median.
Second-half markets are live through the first half: their information set includes the halftime score, foul counts and shooting luck, none of which exists pregame.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game score by period (half), as published for the game; the rules name only 'points scored during the 1st half' so provider hierarchy for the period split is unverified.

mechanism.summary: A first-half contract reads only twenty minutes of play, about 32 to 35 possessions per team, so luck is a larger share of the outcome than in a full game: the half margin has an sd near 7 to 7.5 points against about 10 to 11 for the game, ties occur about 5 percent of the time, and a handful of three-pointers swings the total. Starters, not the bench, play most of the half (around 15 to 17 of the 20 minutes), so the opening lineup, early foul trouble (many coaches sit a player at two first-half fouls) and the coach's substitution pattern determine the real rotation. Pace in a first half differs from the whole-game pace because the second half carries bonus free throws, intentional fouling and clock management. The second-half markets, which are listed over the same game and include overtime, are conditional on the halftime state when traded live, so a halftime update term is required.

stages.name: Opening lineup and first-half rotation
stages.description: Most first-half minutes go to five starters, with the first substitution typically around the 16:00 to 12:00 mark and the bench carrying the late first half. Whether a key starter is playing and when the coach rests him in the half decides the quality of lineups on the floor. Some coaches platoon five-man units, others play starters through the half; the scheme is a coach trait. Starter lists often arrive close to tip.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over rotation scenarios; starters' first-half minutes are bounded in roughly 12 to 20 and positively skewed toward the maximum for stars with no foul trouble.

stages.name: Early foul trouble as a threshold event
stages.description: A player picking up two fouls in the first half is usually benched by cautious coaches for a stretch, which removes a starter exactly when the half's possessions are being decided; the probability depends on the player's foul rate per minute, the opponent's rim-attacking style and the crew's calls. This is a threshold event with a coach policy, not a smooth linear function of the foul rate.
stages.distribution: Binomial-like count of fouls with a policy-driven discrete drop in minutes; per-player probability of two or more first-half fouls ranges from about 10 to 35 percent depending on role and style.

stages.name: First-half possessions and scoring rate
stages.description: First-half possessions are fewer than half of the regulation possessions because the second half carries intentional fouling and bonus stoppages, and teams differ in how fast they start (some are early-offence teams, others walk the ball up). Points per possession in the half follow adjusted offence and defence, but three-point shooting luck over only 30 to 35 possessions is a large share of the variance and does not repeat in the second half.
stages.distribution: Half possessions approximately normal around 32 to 35 per team with sd near 2; half-level points per possession have sd about 15 percent of the mean, with strong three-point luck.

stages.name: Half-end structure and bonus dynamics
stages.description: The last four minutes of a half contain predictable structure: fouls accumulate toward the seventh team foul (one-and-one) and tenth (two shots), the leading team may hold the ball for the last shot, and a two-for-one is possible. Teams with strong free throw shooting and foul-prone defences get more value from this window. It affects the total and the spread by a few points but only the first half has this clock-driven closing structure.
stages.distribution: Late-half scoring is a regime change at the foul-count thresholds; bonus entry timing is stochastic with sd of about 2 minutes.

stages.name: Half margin and tie as a discrete distribution
stages.description: The half margin is an integer random variable with sd about 7 to 7.5 points, centred on roughly 0.55 of the game's expected margin; its pmf has a spike at zero with scoring lumps of 1, 2 and 3 points so that parity effects matter. The tie contract and the spread rungs near zero read this pmf directly, while the half total reads an approximately normal sum. The correlation between half margin and final margin is about 0.7, which makes consistency with game lines a check rather than an input.
stages.distribution: Discrete pmf, near-normal with a central spike; tie probability about 5 percent and a tie-aware spread ladder; second-half margin distribution is wider because of OT and late fouling.

stages.name: Halftime state update for second-half markets
stages.description: Once the first half is over, 2H markets depend on the halftime score and on events in the first half: foul counts of key players, who is in foul trouble, shooting that was far above or below shot quality, and the lead's effect on coaching (lead protection, tempo slowdown). The second-half margin is only weakly related to the halftime margin once strength is known, but the first-half evidence is informative about strength and availability. A pregame-only model cannot price these markets live.
stages.distribution: Conditional distribution: second-half margin has mean pulled toward the pregame expectation (not the halftime lead) with a small slowdown of pace when ahead; additional variance from overtime (5 to 6 percent of games).

opponent_matchup.note: No attached input captures how the opponent's first-half scheme (early foul-drawing, press pressure at the start) changes the half, and no free source gives half-level scheme splits.

role_personnel.note: Starters play most of the half, so who starts and how many minutes they play is first order.

availability_news.note: Opening lineup is announced close to tip; a missing starter has a larger share of effect in a half dominated by starters.

coaching_scheme.note: Substitution timing and the two-foul benching rule are coach policies that drive the first-half rotation.

environment.note: Venue and crowd effects act mostly on the full-game margin and on late-game free throws; no attached or known first-half-specific environment variable is distinguishable from the margin-wide home edge over a 20-minute half.

game_context_script.note: Half-end foul structure and halftime-conditional script are explicit; blowout is relevant to the 2H markets only.

pace_volume.note: First-half possessions differ from half of the game tempo; the ratio is team-specific.

efficiency_conversion.note: Three-point shooting over 30 to 35 possessions drives a large share of half variance.

distribution_variance.note: Integer pmf with a central spike for the tie contract.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, travel and rivalry effects change a team's average effort and fatigue across the game and cannot be separated from noise in a 20-minute half sample of 15 to 30 games per team.
