cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.label: Team first-half possession share and early-game pace ratio
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.mechanism: A team's first-half possessions as a share of its regulation possessions differ from 0.5 because second halves have more fouls and stoppages, and the size of the gap is team and coach specific.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.rationale: Scaling half possessions as half of the game's tempo mis-states the half total and half margin variance; teams that start slowly then accelerate are priced as if their pace were constant.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.measurement: For each team compute r = (1H possessions)/(regulation possessions) per game from period box scores (possessions = FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TO per half), averaged with half-life 15 games and shrunk to the league mean r_lg (about 0.485) with weight n/(n+12); expected 1H possessions = r_team_pair * expected regulation possessions where r_team_pair = average of the two teams' shrunk r; as-of: games before tip.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play for period possession counts
raw_data: per-half field-goal, free-throw, rebound and turnover counts
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.why: Gives a half-specific possession count for 1H total and spread rungs that existing tempo (game level) does not.

cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.label: Coach policy: benching players with early fouls in the first half
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.mechanism: The loss of minutes from early fouls depends on whether the coach sits a starter after two fouls before the break and for how long.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.rationale: Foul rates are stable, but minute loss is a coach decision: some coaches always sit at two fouls, others only after three or when the lead is large. Without this, 'foul trouble risk' is only half a mechanism.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (last 3 seasons) take all starter instances with 2 fouls before the 8:00 mark of the first half; compute P(sit within 2 minutes of the 2nd foul) and the mean minutes missed until return, shrinking each to the league mean with weight n/(n+8); combine with the player's per-minute foul rate (opponent-adjusted) to give expected first-half minutes lost = sum over starters P(2 fouls by time t)*P(sit)*mean_minutes_missed. As-of: through prior game.
raw_data: play-by-play foul events with player id and clock
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.why: Converts foul risk into expected first-half starter minutes, the biggest first-half-specific variance source.

cbb.half_tie_probability.label: Integer pmf and tie probability of the half margin
cbb.half_tie_probability.mechanism: The half margin is an integer with lumps of 1, 2 and 3 points, so its pmf has a central spike and parity structure that a normal density misses.
cbb.half_tie_probability.rationale: KXNCAAMB1H prices a tie as an outcome, and the 1H spread rungs near zero are also affected: each rung difference near 0 equals the pmf at one integer margin; mis-estimating the central mass by half a percentage point is a large error relative to the price.
cbb.half_tie_probability.measurement: Fit a discretized skew-normal or empirical-kernel model for the half margin with mean mu_h = 0.55*E[margin] and sd sigma_h = sqrt(poss_1H/34)*7.2, calibrated on at least 10 seasons of half margins; for tie, compute P(margin = 0) from the pmf with a correction factor c(|mu_h|) estimated from observed ties by expected-margin bucket (|mu| in 0-2, 2-5, 5-9, 9+); as-of: pregame mean and sd.
free_sources: ESPN scoreboard history with half scores
cbb.half_tie_probability.why: Determines the tie contract and the rungs near zero in a way the existing score_resid input (generic residuals) cannot.

cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.label: Halftime state update for second-half markets
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.mechanism: Conditional on the first-half score, foul counts and shooting luck, the second-half margin and total have means shifted away from the pregame values by a small fraction of the first-half residual.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.rationale: The 2H series are live markets over the same game. The pregame prior plus an update on the halftime state is the correct information set, and the update is not 'trust the lead': most of a first-half lead is luck, but foul trouble and injuries are real.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.measurement: Regress second-half margin on pregame expected margin, 1H margin residual (1H margin minus 0.55*pregame expected), starters in foul trouble indicator (2+ fouls for a top-5 player), team foul counts, 1H 3P% minus expected, and an injury-in-game flag, using at least 5 seasons of halftime states; output conditional mean and sd of 2H margin and total (including OT mixture). Typical expected coefficient on the 1H residual: 0.1 to 0.25. Not available pregame; knowable at halftime.
raw_data: first-half score, fouls by player, shooting splits
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.why: The 2H winner, spread and total series cannot be priced from pregame inputs alone once the market trades through halftime.

cbb.half_split.reason: Team-specific first-half share of scoring is mostly noise over 30 games; useful only as a heavily shrunk effect and not as a primary feature, and it overlaps with the new pace ratio.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions drive the half total, but game tempo is a poor proxy for first-half possessions (about 48.5 percent of the game); needs the half ratio.

cbb.starters.reason: In a half dominated by starters, the lineup announcement is first order; correctly primary but arrives near tip.

cbb.first_half_minutes.reason: Historical starters' first-half minutes anchor the rotation; overlaps with player foul trouble so should be modelled jointly.

cbb.adj_off.reason: Full-game adjusted offence is the scoring base, with a half-level conversion needed; secondary because first-half luck dominates.

cbb.adj_def.reason: Same reason as adjusted offence: the base rate for the half, with large half-specific noise.

cbb.half_foul_bonus.reason: Bonus entry timing and end-of-half possession structure are real half-specific mechanics with a modest effect size.

cbb.player_foul.reason: Early foul-trouble minute risk is already stated in the first-half minutes entry; the player-level foul rate is the feature behind it, so both should be one concept feeding the new coach bench rule.

cbb.injuries.reason: Mislabelled as secondary relative to its true effect in a starter-heavy half, but disclosure is thin, so keep with scenario mixture.

cbb.score_resid.reason: Generic residual shape; the half needs its own integer pmf (tie mass) so this is background only.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path after the lineup announcement; shows what the market priced but is not a driver of first-half scoring.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines half-only points, the tie contract and OT inclusion for 2H; these are the labels.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook first-half lines are mostly derived from the game line; they are the comparison, not an input.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Half total, half spread and game lines must agree; checking this against quotes is a market diagnostic and not an outcome input.

cbb.roster_minutes.reason: Rotation depth determines how the starters' minutes in the half are distributed, but its information is mostly contained in first-half minutes.

cbb.three_pt_luck.reason: In 20 minutes a few threes swing the total; regression of recent shooting toward shot quality is useful, although the half effect is noisy.

interactions.mechanism: First-half scoring equals first-half possessions times first-half points per possession; a team that starts fast (high half pace ratio) and shoots above shot quality early gets the product of both advantages, while the second half is not affected, so the effect lives only in the half contract.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress first-half points on adjusted tempo, half pace ratio, and their product while controlling for the game total; check whether the product term adds out-of-sample power.

interactions.mechanism: A star starter's early foul trouble costs minutes only if the coach sits at two fouls, and costs more if the replacement is a much weaker unit; the net first-half impact is the product of foul probability, benching policy and the gap between starter and substitute.
interactions.how_to_test: Using historical games with a starter at two first-half fouls, compare the half margin shift by coach policy bucket and replacement gap.

interactions.mechanism: Once a team reaches the seventh foul in the half its opponent gets one-and-one chances and at the tenth two shots, so the value of each additional foul steps up; teams with 75 percent or better free-throw shooters gain much more than poor ones, producing a threshold-by-skill interaction late in the half.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare points per possession in the last four minutes of the first half in bonus versus pre-bonus states split by team free-throw percentage tercile.

interactions.mechanism: For 2H contracts that include overtime, the second-half margin distribution is a mixture of the regulation second half and the overtime period, and the probability of reaching overtime depends on the halftime margin and the pregame expectation together; a halftime lead of 15 nearly removes the OT component.

interactions.mechanism: Because the first half has about 33 possessions, a hot or cold shooting start is a larger share of the half outcome for slow teams that have fewer possessions, so the regression weight on recent shooting luck should rise as the expected half possession count falls.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether the sensitivity of 1H points to last-10-game 3P% deviation differs between slow-starting and fast-starting teams.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at two first-half fouls with a coach-dependent step down in minutes
nonlinearities.why: Minutes lost are zero until the second foul and then drop by 4 to 8 minutes in the half, so the expected cost is not proportional to the foul rate; the discontinuity at the second foul produces an asymmetric variance contribution.

nonlinearities.shape: step increase in free-throw value at the 7th and 10th team fouls
nonlinearities.why: Each foul before the bonus gives a side-out, each foul after gives one or two shots; the scoring yield of the final minutes of the half therefore jumps non-linearly in team fouls, particularly for good free-throw teams.

nonlinearities.shape: peaked discrete pmf at zero decaying with expected-margin magnitude; not Gaussian near zero
nonlinearities.why: A tie needs an exact integer margin of 0 given lumps of 1 to 3 points; its probability falls from about 5.5 percent for even teams to under 3 percent when the expected half margin is above 8, a shape that a normal with equal sd mis-estimates at the centre.

contract.settlement_definition: No rules text was sampled for the four live series (KXNCAAMBFIRST10, FIRST25, FIRST50, RACE: 'Race to N Points', titles only), so settlement details are unknown. The archetype target is a player's points over a half-point strike, which would settle on the official box score of the named game; whether regulation only or overtime counts, what a player who does not play (DNP) does to the market (void or NO), and the source of the player statistic are not visible. The live series are titled 'Race to N points', which may be first team (or first player) to reach N points, a different event from a single-player ladder; the ledger classifies them as player_prop:points but the title does not establish who races.
variants_and_edge_cases: Race-to-N markets (10, 25, 50 points) are first-to-reach events: if team-level they depend on early-game scoring pace and who wins the opening possession; if player-level they depend on who takes the first shots and whether that player is in the starting lineup. The sampled titles do not say which.
A player points-over strike is a count threshold on a discrete variable (integer, overdispersed); rung spacing and whether 'N+' or 'over N.5' construction is used cannot be verified.

DNP handling is the first-order unknown for any player prop: if a DNP resolves to NO rather than void, availability probability is a multiplicative term in every YES price; if void, availability drops out of the label but not the information set.
Overtime: a game that goes to extra time adds about 3 to 4 points to a starter's expected total in 5 to 6 percent of games; whether these count is not stated.
College rosters can add or remove a player for non-injury reasons (eligibility rulings, suspension, transfer) between listing and tip, which behaves like a DNP with little warning.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in any sampled text. Likely the official box score (NCAA or school statistician), with ESPN/Sports-Reference as secondary, but the rules do not say so; box-score corrections after the final can change a player's points by one or two.

mechanism.summary: Points are minutes times shot attempts per minute times points per attempt plus free-throw points, a chain in which each stage is stochastic and several are strongly coupled to the game's script. Whether and how long the player plays is a mixture: availability (DNP, minute restrictions), foul trouble (a threshold event), and blowout truncation that makes minutes bimodal for starters on heavy favourites. Shot volume follows usage, pace and the teammates on the floor (absences redistribute shots to remaining scorers at lower efficiency), and conversion depends on shot quality, opponent defence, and a large luck component that should be shrunk hard to talent over 30 games. Late free throws in close games add points for ball handlers. The result is an overdispersed integer distribution with a zero or very low component for non-participation, a heavy right tail from hot nights, and contract rungs (such as 25+ points) that sit in that tail.

stages.name: Participation: plays, starts, or does not
stages.description: Before any rate matters, the player must be on the floor. College teams publish little injury information, so a starter's status is often learned at warm-ups, and transfers or eligibility issues can change a roster without notice. The scenario set is {plays full role, plays restricted, does not play}, and the settlement rule for a non-appearance decides whether this stage is a void or a NO.
stages.distribution: Mixture with a small point mass at zero (DNP, typically 3 to 8 percent for a listed starter in a long season) and a restricted-minutes component for players returning from injury.

stages.name: Minutes as a state-dependent distribution
stages.description: Starters average 28 to 35 minutes but the realised minutes depend on the game state: in a blowout starters sit after about 30 to 32 minutes of lead time, in a close game they play 36 or more, and early foul trouble (two in the first half, four in the second) cuts minutes by a coach-specific rule. The expected minutes are therefore not a single number but a mixture whose weights depend on the spread and on foul risk, so a high points rung is much more sensitive to the probability of a competitive game than the mean suggests.
stages.distribution: Minutes are bimodal for stars on big favourites (about 25 versus 34), truncated at 40 plus overtime; foul trouble creates a long left tail.

stages.name: Shot attempts per minute: usage, pace and teammates
stages.description: Field-goal attempts per minute equal the player's usage share of team possessions times the game's pace, redistributed by who else is on the floor. When a primary scorer is out, remaining scorers take more shots but at lower efficiency because the shots are harder, and the effect depends on whether the replacement is a same-role scorer or a different type. Opponent style (zone versus man) changes the shot distribution by role.
stages.distribution: Shot count per game is overdispersed relative to Poisson (variance about 1.5 to 2 times mean), and strongly correlated with minutes and with team pace.

stages.name: Conversion: points per attempt with large luck
stages.description: Points per attempt depend on shot mix (rim, mid-range, three-point), shot quality and the opponent's defence, but a large part of a player's season percentage is luck: three-point percentage over 150 attempts has a sampling sd near 4 percentage points, comparable to real differences between shooters. The right expected conversion is a shrunk estimate that combines the player's own record, his shot locations and a prior by role.
stages.distribution: Binomial-like conversion with hierarchical shrinkage; per-game points per attempt has an sd of 0.25 to 0.35, much of it unforecastable.

stages.name: Free-throw trips and late-game script
stages.description: Free-throw points come from drawn fouls during play and from the closing minutes of close games when the trailing team fouls and ball handlers take the shots. A guard on a team leading in a close game can add 4 to 8 points in the last two minutes. The trips depend on the player's drawn-foul rate against the opponent's foul propensity and on whether the game is within reach. This part of the distribution is a heavy tail from close games, not a smooth rate.
stages.distribution: Free-throw attempts per game for a guard are overdispersed with a zero-inflated closing component; FT% per game has an sd near 15 points.

stages.name: Count distribution, race variants and settlement
stages.description: The player's points are an integer total with a variance greater than a Poisson of the same mean because the stages above are positively correlated (minutes drive attempts drive points), plus the participation mixture. High rungs depend on the tail shape, and the correlation of points with game total and margin matters if the contract is part of a parlay. For the Race-to-N variants, the quantity is the time or order at which scoring reaches N, which depends on early-game scoring pace and the opening lineup rather than on the total.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed negative-binomial-like count with a mass at zero; race events are first-passage times with start-of-game dependence.

cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture by game state and foul risk
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: A player's minutes are a mixture of at least three regimes (competitive full minutes, blowout truncated, foul-trouble truncated) with weights set by the spread, the coach's rotation habits and the foul propensity.
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: A single expected-minutes number averages a bimodal variable; for a star on a 15-point favourite the 28-minute mode and the 34-minute mode generate very different probabilities of reaching 25 points, so the mixture matters more for high rungs than for the median.
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: Fit for each player-role bucket (starter guard, starter wing, starter big, rotation) a three-component model on minutes: component weights w_k = softmax(a_k + b_k*|expected margin| + c_k*foul_rate_per_40 + d_k*back-to-back flag), with component means estimated from last two seasons of games per coach with ridge shrinkage; output the pmf over minutes in 4-minute bins; as-of: spread-free (use model expected margin, not market line).
raw_data: final margin and pregame expected margin
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.why: Supplies the discrete minutes distribution that determines high-rung probabilities for points; the existing player_minutes entry is a single projection.

cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.label: Location-based expected points per shot attempt with opponent adjustment
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.mechanism: A player's expected points per attempt equals the sum over shot locations of attempt share times league-average make rate times value, adjusted for the opponent's defence at each location.
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.rationale: Observed FG% is a noisy estimate; shot location (rim, short mid-range, long two, three, catch-and-shoot versus off-dribble) predicts future efficiency better than recent results, and regression should move the observed rate toward the location-implied rate rather than toward a flat league mean.
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.measurement: xPPS = sum_z share_z * (league_make_z shrunk with player make_z weight n_z/(n_z+60)) * value_z + FT component; opponent adjustment: multiply each zone's rate by (opponent allowed rate in zone / league rate)^0.5 estimated over the last 20 games with half-life 8; as-of: through prior game; units points per shot attempt.
free_sources: hoop-math.com shot-location tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for current coverage)
raw_data: player shot attempts and makes by zone
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.why: Replaces a per-percentage regression with a model-based expectation so that hot-and-cold streaks are discounted correctly for each player's shot profile.

cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.label: Player expected free-throw attempts: drawn-foul rate and late-game ball-handling share
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.mechanism: Player FTA equal drawn fouls per 100 possessions times possessions on court times a bonus factor, plus a late-game component for ball handlers on teams likely to lead or to be fouled at the end.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.rationale: Free throws are a distinct scoring channel with its own distribution; late-game trips depend on the probability of a close game and on who handles the ball, so guards and wings differ even at equal usage.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.measurement: xFTA = (drawn-foul FTA rate per 100 on-court possessions, last 20 games, half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+8) to role mean) * expected on-court possessions + P(close at 2:00 left) * (ball-handler share of late possessions) * expected late FTA per team (about 4 in a one-possession game); FT% enters separately with shrinkage n/(n+100) to 72 percent league mean; as-of: pregame.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player FTA and fouls drawn (derive)
raw_data: player FTA per game with minutes
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.why: Isolates a heavy-tailed scoring channel specific to guards that the team-level free-throw input cannot represent.

cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.label: Player points dispersion index by role
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.mechanism: Variance of a player's single-game points relative to his mean varies by role (high-usage guard versus low-usage big) and by shot mix.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.rationale: High rungs (25 plus) read the tail of the count distribution, and the tail width depends on role variance more than on the mean; using one dispersion for all players mis-prices the high and low rungs in opposite directions.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.measurement: For each role bucket compute phi = var(points | minutes bucket, expected usage) / mean over the last 3 seasons of player games with weight to the player's own phi_i = n/(n+25) shrinkage; use negative binomial with mean mu and size r = mu/(phi-1) conditional on playing 15+ minutes, mixed with the DNP point mass; output per-rung probabilities; as-of: pregame.
raw_data: player points per game with minutes
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.why: Provides the shape used by every points rung and the tail used by 25+ and 30+ thresholds.

cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.label: Early-game scoring profile and opening-possession edge for race-to-N markets
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.mechanism: A race to N points is a first-passage problem: the leader after the opening minutes is determined by the opening lineup's scoring rate, the tip or arrow possession and early turnovers.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.rationale: The ledger classifies the only live series (Race to 10, 25, 50) in this archetype, but a first-passage event depends on points per possession in the first 8 to 12 minutes with starters, not on full-game efficiency; race to 50 additionally integrates to about the 28th to 30th minute and is affected by the substitution pattern.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.measurement: From play-by-play compute per team the time series of cumulative points in the first 10, 25 and 50 point marks (minutes to reach each), as-of prior games with half-life 12 games; model lambda_A, lambda_B as points per possession of the starters' unit in the first 8 minutes (with shrinkage n/(n+10) to full-game ppp); P(A first to N) from a Skellam-type random walk in possessions with a first-possession edge of about 0.5 possession (tip or arrow, 50 percent) added; as-of: before tip, with lineup status.
free_sources: NCAA live stats archive (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk)
raw_data: play-by-play with clock and score by team
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.why: Specific to the only live series in the archetype; first-to-N events are not predicted by player points per game.

cbb.player_usage.reason: Usage share of possessions is the stable driver of attempts; it must be role- and lineup-conditional, since usage changes when teammates are out.

cbb.player_minutes.reason: Minutes are the largest multiplier, but a single projection hides the bimodality from blowouts and foul trouble; combine with the scenario mixture.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Redistribution of shots when scorers are out is a real, large effect; its efficiency penalty must be modelled separately from the volume gain.

cbb.player_shooting_regression.reason: Shot-making luck is the main source of forecast error in points; regression is essential and should use shot location.

cbb.free_throw.reason: Described as FT rate and FT% 'for player' but it is a team-level catalog input; for a player prop the drawn-foul rate and late-game handling are needed.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.reason: Opponent points allowed by role has tiny samples (a few games per role per team) and mostly reflects team defence and pace; keep only as a shrunk adjustment.

cbb.defense_style.reason: Zone and press shift shot types by role, but size of effect on one player's points is smaller than minutes uncertainty.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions scale attempts proportionally; not primary because the game pace has less leverage than minutes and role.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: State variable that truncates star minutes; needed as a probability, not as a flag.

cbb.player_foul.reason: Foul-trouble risk matters at the threshold of two first-half fouls; the coach rule is the missing half of the mechanism.

cbb.injuries.reason: Availability of the player and of teammates; the biggest discrete driver, constrained by disclosure.

m.quote_history.reason: Price movements are a timing diagnostic, not a determinant of the player's points.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the DNP rule and the stat source for labels; critical because no text was sampled.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook player points lines are the comparison prior; using them as an input would hide model deviations.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Check of quote monotonicity across rungs; market-derived and not an outcome input.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Historical realised frequency by rung from past Kalshi settlements measures market calibration; not a driver of player points.

cbb.late_game_foul_script.reason: Late free throws by ball handlers are a real tail source; the effect is concentrated in close games and for guards.

interactions.mechanism: When a primary scorer is out, a remaining scorer's usage rises but his efficiency falls because the extra shots are lower quality and defences key on him; the net points gain flattens (or even reverses) as usage climbs beyond about 28 percent, particularly if the replacement is not a same-role scorer.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with a missing top scorer compare player points per shot at baseline usage and at high usage; fit points = usage * efficiency(usage) and test for concavity.

interactions.mechanism: For a starter on a favourite, the chance of crossing a high points rung is dominated by the probability of staying in a competitive game; in the blowout regime minutes drop by about 8 and points by about 6, so the high rung is a mixture and lower rungs are relatively insensitive.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare probability of 20 plus points among starters in games with predicted margin above and below 12, holding usage fixed; the gap should be larger at high rungs than at lower rungs.

interactions.mechanism: Attempts equal usage share times team possessions, so a high-usage player in a fast game has a multiplicative boost to volume and variance, in a way that an additive tempo term cannot capture for large usage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress player FGA on tempo, usage and their product, using games from the previous two seasons, and compare against the no-product model.

interactions.mechanism: Late free throws accrue only if the game stays within about six points inside the last two minutes and only to the ball handlers on the floor, so the contribution is a step function of closeness times role, nearly zero for bigs and for blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by margin at 2:00 and compare late free throws by position; confirm a step in the 0-6 point bucket for guards.

interactions.mechanism: The weight on observed shooting streaks relative to the shot-location expectation should fall as the number of attempts grows and rise when the player's shot mix changed (new role or new team), so the regression target is conditional on sample size and on role change.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare out-of-sample prediction of next-game points per attempt using observed-only, xPPS-only and blended estimates stratified by attempts to date and by role change flags.

nonlinearities.shape: bimodal mixture with a threshold in expected margin: minutes drop sharply beyond a lead of about 15
nonlinearities.why: Points are nearly proportional to minutes, but minutes are not a smooth function of the spread; the jump between a competitive game and a bench-clearing blowout creates a discontinuity in the probability of reaching high rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: step at two first-half fouls and again at four total fouls, coach-dependent
nonlinearities.why: A second foul before halftime usually produces an immediate benching and a third a longer one, so lost minutes jump rather than rising proportionally to the foul rate, creating a heavy left tail in minutes and points.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: usage gain with falling efficiency, saturating around high usage
nonlinearities.why: The first extra shots come at near baseline quality, later ones are contested attempts, so marginal points per extra attempt decline; a linear usage-redistribution model overstates the remaining scorers' production when a star is out.

contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists in the ledger for this generic archetype, so there is no rules text to verify. The intended contract is a single named player's counting statistic (points, rebounds, assists, threes, or a combination) over a half-point or integer threshold in one game, settling on the official box score. What a player who does not play does to the market (void, NO, or YES for an 'under' side), whether overtime counts, how combination stats are summed, and which box-score provider is the source of truth are all unspecified and must not be inferred from the other CBB series.
variants_and_edge_cases: Combination props (points plus rebounds plus assists, double-double) multiply the number of stats that must settle correctly and make the provider choice and the correlation between stats first order.
Rung construction can be over/under a .5 line or an 'N or more' ladder; for a discrete count the two have identical probabilities only if the strike set is the same integer.

A player who is on the roster but does not play (injury, coach's decision, suspension, eligibility) is a DNP whose label is undefined; a player who plays three minutes is a technical appearance with almost no counting stats.
Stat corrections: college box scores for smaller venues can be edited after the game (assist credited, rebound reassigned), so the first published value may differ from the settled one.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not defined (no rules text). Candidates are the official NCAA statistician's box score, ESPN, or Sports-Reference; discrepancies between them for assists and rebounds are known to exist, with a typical difference of one unit for a few percent of players.

mechanism.summary: Any counting prop is a latent player state multiplied through a common chain: does the player appear, how many minutes and in what role, how many opportunities per minute for the particular stat, and how many of those convert, with the box score as a measured (not true) record. The shared layer is what makes the generic archetype different from any single stat: availability and minutes are common to every stat, role (ball handler, wing, big) selects which stats have large rates, and the stats are correlated through minutes and game script, so combination props and parlays need a joint distribution. College adds three specific difficulties: samples of about 30 games with partial role changes, transfer-portal players with no history at the new team, and box-score statistics recorded by a home scorekeeper with variable quality.

stages.name: Appearance and the cause of non-appearance
stages.description: A prop is only meaningful if the player plays, and the probability of playing depends on why a player might not: a confirmed injury differs from an unannounced coach's decision or an eligibility ruling, and each has a different pregame signal and a different time at which the information appears. College disclosure is voluntary, so many non-appearances are surprises. The settlement rule (void or NO) decides whether this stage affects the label or only the information set.
stages.distribution: Point mass at zero for DNP (a few percent for starters, much higher for rotation players) plus a restricted-minutes component after injury.

stages.name: Role and minutes as a latent state
stages.description: Role (starter guard, wing, stretch big, rim runner) determines both the minutes envelope and which stats have large per-minute rates. Minutes depend on the rotation size, foul trouble and the probability of a blowout, and they are common to every statistic of the same player, so a minute shortfall hits points, rebounds and assists together. A shorter rotation concentrates minutes in the starters and reduces variance for them.
stages.distribution: Minutes distribution is truncated at 40 (plus overtime) with a heavy left tail from foul trouble and blowouts; position and role shift the mean by up to 10 minutes.

stages.name: Per-minute rates with hierarchical shrinkage and cold starts
stages.description: Per-minute counting rates are estimated from 30 or fewer games, with role changes between seasons and for transfers, so the estimate is a hierarchical posterior combining the player's own record, the role's prior and, for newcomers, the prior-team production translated through team quality and position. Teammate absences shift rates for the remaining players, and the effective sample size is smaller than the games played count because the role has changed.
stages.distribution: Rates have between-game overdispersion; posterior sd of the true rate is about 15 to 25 percent of the mean for players with fewer than 15 games in the current role.

stages.name: Opponent, pace and joint dependence between stats
stages.description: Opponent style changes the opportunity supply (opponent three-point volume, rebound opportunities, turnover pressure), and game pace scales every stat. The stats of one player are correlated: rebounds and points covary through minutes and in a fast game all counts rise. Combination markets and any parlay of two props from the same player need the joint distribution, which is not the product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between stats through shared minutes and pace (around 0.3 to 0.5 for points with rebounds in raw counts, falling after conditioning on minutes); the dependence is non-Gaussian in the tails.

stages.name: Measurement: how the box score records the stat
stages.description: The settled value is a recorded statistic, not the underlying count. Assists, steals, blocks and sometimes rebounds depend on the statistician's judgement; a home-court scorekeeper effect has been documented in professional basketball and plausibly exists in college, where scorers are volunteers or students at smaller venues. Late corrections change values after the fact.
stages.distribution: Small measurement noise with possible venue-specific bias (up to a few percent of the mean for assists and blocks), concentrated in non-power-conference venues.

stages.name: Distribution form and ladder mapping
stages.description: Counting stats are discrete with different shapes: points are overdispersed, rebounds and assists closer to Poisson with zero inflation for low-minute players, threes made are a thinned Poisson (attempts times make probability). A ladder reads the cumulative tail, so the dispersion and the zero mass matter more than the mean for extreme rungs. Overtime adds a small mixture.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial or zero-inflated forms with stat-specific dispersion; cumulative probabilities across rungs are monotone and must be consistent with the minutes mixture.

talent_strength.note: Per-minute rates with shrinkage and a cold-start prior for transfers.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent opportunity supply by role; small samples, so priors are important.

role_personnel.note: Role selects the stats and sets the effective sample for shrinkage.

availability_news.note: Participation split by cause; disclosure is voluntary in college.

coaching_scheme.note: Rotation size and foul-benching rules are coach choices; direct coach-level tendencies are inferred from past minutes only.

environment.note: Arena and weather conditions act on team-level pace and home advantage, which enter through tempo; no environmental variable acts on a single player's stat line beyond them in the known data.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and close-game states truncate or extend the minutes of the same player for all stats.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion regression for shooting stats; non-shooting stats rely on rate shrinkage.

distribution_variance.note: Marginal shapes and cross-stat dependence for combination markets.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: A single game's rest and travel effect on one player's counting stats is smaller than the sampling noise of 30 games and no stable player-level effect is known; rotation changes from schedule are captured by roster minutes.

officiating_rules.note: The crew affects fouls and thereby minutes; official scorers affect recorded assists and blocks.

settlement_contract.note: No live series and no rules text exist for generic college player props, so DNP handling, OT, source of truth and rung construction are undefined; the archetype cannot be evaluated against a contract.

cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.label: Cold-start role and rate prior for transfer and freshman players
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.mechanism: A player new to a team has no history in the current system; his minutes, usage and per-minute rates must be inferred from previous team production translated through quality and position gaps.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.rationale: Because a large share of D1 rotation minutes (a figure to be measured, not assumed) is carried each year by transfers and freshmen new to their team, early-season props for newcomers are priced on prior-team averages even though role and competition change; the translation is non-trivial and is the largest source of early-season error.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.measurement: For each newcomer with prior-season D1 stats: prior usage = prev_usage * (prev_team_ORtg_rank / new_team_ORtg_rank)^0.3 shrunk toward the new team's open-minutes distribution by weight depending on departures (minutes available = minutes of lost players / 200); per-minute rate prior = prev rate * conference-strength factor (from the KenPom/Torvik conference ratings gap; the per-tier discount, assumed between 3 and 8 percent, is to be calibrated) + position adjustment; replace with current-season rates as n/(n+10 games). For freshmen use recruiting rank (247 composite) mapped to expected BPM from history. As-of: portal status and roster at the decision time.
free_sources: 247Sports composite and portal tracker (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk export)
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.why: Without it the generic props archetype has no estimate for the largest group of college players with unreliable histories.

cbb.player_stat_covariance.label: Cross-stat covariance of points, rebounds, assists and threes within a player
cbb.player_stat_covariance.mechanism: Stats of the same player are positively correlated through minutes, pace and game state, with a residual correlation after conditioning that depends on role.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.rationale: Combination markets and parlays require the joint probability; independence overstates variance reduction and misprices points-plus-rebounds style thresholds in the tails.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.measurement: Estimate the 4x4 correlation of Pearson residuals of (points, rebounds, assists, threes) given expected minutes by role bucket using the last 3 seasons, shrink each correlation toward the role bucket pooled value with weight n/(n+40); simulate via a Gaussian copula with stat-specific NB marginals conditioned on a shared minutes draw from the minutes mixture; as-of: prior games.
raw_data: per-game stat lines with minutes for each player
cbb.player_stat_covariance.why: Defines how combination and multi-prop contracts are priced; absent from the marginal-only stat_dist input.

cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.label: Role-stable effective sample size for shrinkage
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.mechanism: Games played in a different role (injury return, new starter, teammate absence) carry less information about today's rate than games in the same role.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.rationale: Shrinkage constants set by raw game counts under-shrink players whose role changed and over-shrink stable ones; hierarchical estimates need the effective, not nominal, sample.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.measurement: n_eff = sum over prior games g of w_g where w_g = exp(-age_g/12 games) * (1 if |minutes_g - expected minutes now| < 6 and starter flag matches else 0.4) * (1 if teammate availability set matches within one starter else 0.7); shrinkage factor k/(n_eff + k) with k = 12 games for rebounds, 20 for points, 30 for threes made; as-of: through prior game.
raw_data: player game log with starter flag and minutes
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.why: Controls how much of a small-sample average is trusted for each stat for each player.

cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.label: Home-venue scorekeeper bias in recorded assists, blocks and rebounds
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.mechanism: The official statistician's discretion on assists, steals and blocks varies by venue; the same player's recorded rate differs at home versus away after controlling for his true activity.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.rationale: If a home venue systematically credits more assists, an over on assists is cheaper at home than the rate suggests; the effect is stable and cheap to estimate from the difference between home and away rates of visitors.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.measurement: For each arena compute (assists per 100 team FGM recorded for the home team minus the same teams' away rate) minus league mean home gap, using 3 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+300 team games); likewise blocks per 100 opponent two-point attempts; apply as a multiplicative adjustment capped at +/-6 percent; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED that the effect exists in college data at this size.
raw_data: home and away team assists, blocks, FGM, opponent FGA by game and venue
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.why: Specific to measurement of non-shooting stats; points are unaffected.

cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.label: Cause-specific non-appearance probabilities (injury, coach decision, eligibility, suspension)
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.mechanism: Different causes of absence have different base rates, different warning signals and different timing, so a single status probability mixes unlike events.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.rationale: College players miss games for reasons that never appear in an injury list (coach's decision, academic or eligibility issues, return from injury minutes limits); treating all absences alike loses the signal that a long-listed injury is more informative than a quiet scratch.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.measurement: Classify historical non-appearances of rotation players (top-8 minutes) into causes using news and box score patterns; estimate P(appear) = 1 - sum_c P(cause_c | status label, days since status, program type) with Beta priors by cause (for example injury questionable: 0.55 play; undisclosed: 0.97 play) updated weekly; as-of: status vintage; output also restricted-minutes probability after return (minutes cap 20 in first game back).
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.why: Gives the participation probability the minutes mixture requires and keeps injury, decision and eligibility absences separate.

cbb.player_minutes.reason: Minutes are the common multiplier across every stat; must be a distribution conditional on spread and foul risk rather than a point projection.

cbb.player_usage.reason: Per-minute opportunity rate by stat, with role-specific priors; the label bundles shooting, rebounding and assist rates, which should be split by stat.

cbb.injuries.reason: Participation of the player and teammates; value depends on knowing the cause and timing.

cbb.status_disclosure.reason: Calibrated play probability by status label is useful, but college label vocabulary is inconsistent and the sample is small.

cbb.starters.reason: Confirmed starters arrive around tip, after many markets have closed; downgraded from primary because it is rarely available in the tradable window.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Redistribution is a large and real effect, but is capped at role-appropriate transfers and needs with/without sample guards.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions scale all stats proportionally; second order next to minutes and role.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: State variable that truncates minutes and thereby every stat; essential for tails.

cbb.player_foul.reason: Foul trouble is a threshold effect on minutes; incomplete without the coach benching policy.

cbb.player_role_position.reason: Mislabelled secondary: role determines which stat distributions matter and which opponent adjustment applies; it is the index for the whole hierarchy.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.reason: Opponent allowed by role has tiny samples and largely duplicates team style and pace; use only with strong shrinkage.

cbb.stat_dist.reason: Marginal count shapes and parameter uncertainty define every rung; needs a joint extension for combination props.

cbb.player_shooting_regression.reason: Relevant for shooting stats (points, threes) and not for rebounds or assists; secondary for the generic archetype.

cbb.box_score_source_risk.reason: Provider lag and error affect labels and timing; it is a settlement risk and not a driver of the stat itself.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook prop lines are the comparison prior; using them as an input hides model edge.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of quotes; a market-side check only.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Execution capacity, no information about the outcome.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Historical market hit rates by rung are a calibration artefact of past quotes, not a driver of the stat.

m.volume_oi.reason: Liquidity of a prop market does not inform a player's statistics.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Labels and timing of settled values; critical for backtests but not a predictor.

cbb.market_calibration_bias.reason: Describes market miscalibration by price bucket; a post-model shading and not an input.

cbb.roster_minutes.reason: Rotation size and minutes concentration determine how absences redistribute minutes; overlaps partly with player minutes but gives the team-level constraint.

interactions.mechanism: When a starter is out, remaining starters absorb the minutes only if the rotation is short; in a deep rotation the freed minutes go to bench players, so the stat redistribution to any given teammate is conditional on the rotation's depth and on whether the missing player was a ball handler or a big.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with a missing starter, regress teammate minute and stat change on the missing player's minutes share interacted with a bench-depth index (minutes of players 6 to 9).

interactions.mechanism: The correct dispersion of a player's stat depends on how many role-stable games underlie the estimate: with few such games the posterior uncertainty adds to the sampling variance, widening the distribution and moving probability mass to both tails of the ladder.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare calibration of rung probabilities from a fixed-dispersion model against one with n_eff-dependent dispersion, stratified by n_eff terciles.

interactions.mechanism: A shortfall in minutes lowers every stat at once, so unconditional correlations between points, rebounds and assists are mostly due to minutes; after conditioning the residual correlation is small or even negative (points and assists compete for the same possessions for a guard), so joint props need the shared minutes draw plus a residual copula.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed joint frequencies of two-stat thresholds with simulated joints from independent-given-minutes versus copula-with-residual models.

interactions.mechanism: A scorekeeper's generosity matters only for judgement-based stats, so it adds to assists for ball handlers and blocks for rim protectors but leaves points untouched; the role selects which adjustment applies, and it matters more at small-conference venues than at power-conference ones with professional statisticians.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate home minus away assist-rate gap by role and by conference tier and check that it differs from zero only for ball handlers and non-power venues.

interactions.mechanism: A starter's minutes fall once the expected game margin exceeds the coach's blowout trigger (a lead of 20 with eight to ten minutes left); the drop applies to every stat, and its depth is larger for scorers who sit than for rebounders who may be left in longer, so each stat has its own threshold response.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare minutes and stat per 36 by expected-margin bucket for starters on favourites and underdogs; look for a break near 15 expected points.

nonlinearities.shape: variance-to-mean ratio varies with the mean and minutes; zero inflation increases for players with fewer than 15 minutes
nonlinearities.why: Counts for low-minute players are close to a degenerate distribution near zero while those of stars are approximately Poisson-plus-overdispersion, so a single dispersion parameter distorts both the tails and the probability of exceeding 0.5 for bench players.

nonlinearities.shape: non-monotone mapping of status label to play probability with a mass near 0.5 for 'questionable' and near 0.95 for undisclosed
nonlinearities.why: A label of questionable is about as likely to mean out as in, whereas silence usually means he plays; the mapping from label to probability is a step function that depends on program and time to tip, not a smooth severity scale.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at about 15 minutes below which counts collapse; approximately linear above
nonlinearities.why: A player who is limited to under 15 minutes produces few counting stats, while above that threshold output scales near-proportionally to minutes, so the distribution has a kink and a spike at low minutes.

contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists in the ledger for college player rebounds or assists, so no rules text can be read. The intended contract is one named player's total rebounds or total assists (separate props, possibly also a rebounds-plus-assists combination) over a half-point threshold in one game, settled from the official box score. Treatment of a non-appearance, of overtime, of how a combination is summed, and of which statistician or provider is authoritative cannot be established from any sampled text and is therefore unverified; it is not assumed to match the points or full-game series.
variants_and_edge_cases: Rebounds in college box scores include offensive and defensive rebounds by the player but team rebounds (deadball, shot-clock violations) are credited to the team, so total board counts differ across providers by whether team rebounds are included in the team line.

Assists are a judgement of the official scorer (a pass leading directly to a basket), with a recognised range of scorer discretion between venues; an assist threshold such as 7.5 is therefore sensitive to who keeps the book.

A rebounds-plus-assists combination couples two stats that are negatively related through game shooting (hot shooting lifts assists, lowers rebounds), so the combination variance is lower than the sum of variances for guards.
Overtime adds about five minutes of play for the starters in 5 to 6 percent of games, lifting expected counts by about 12 to 15 percent in those games; whether overtime counts is undefined.
contract.settlement_data_source: Undefined. Official NCAA box score from the home statistician is the likely source; provider differences for assists and rebounds are a documented issue in college where volunteer or student statisticians are used at smaller programmes (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for magnitude).

mechanism.summary: Rebounds and assists are the two stats in which a player's production depends mostly on what teammates and opponents do, not on his own shooting. A rebound is a share of a finite pool of misses (both teams' misses, split offensive and defensive), with the player's share determined by who else is on the floor competing for the same boards, his positioning and the location and length of the missed shots; an assist is a credit for a teammate's made basket, so it is the product of the player's opportunity to create (ball-handling share), teammates' shot-making (largely luck game to game) and the scorer's discretion. Both scale with minutes and pace, and both move in opposite directions with game shooting luck (hot shooting means fewer rebounds and more assists), which makes the two stats a negatively dependent pair and gives each a different sensitivity to blowouts and lineup changes than points.

stages.name: Minutes and the lineup he shares the floor with
stages.description: Both stats are earned during minutes on the floor, but what matters for rebounds is who else is there: two bigs split the boards while one big alone collects them, and a small-ball unit gives guards more rebounding chances. For assists, whether the player or a teammate is the primary handler on the floor controls the creation share. Minutes themselves are truncated by foul trouble and blowouts, and lineups shift when a starter is missing.
stages.distribution: Minutes as a bounded mixture (blowout, foul trouble); lineup composition is a discrete set of the team's common five-man units with probabilities depending on availability.

stages.name: Supply of rebounds: misses, their location and who collects
stages.description: The pool is total missed field goals and live missed free throws by both teams in the minutes played, which rises with pace and with poor shooting. The split between offensive and defensive rebounds depends on the teams' crashing versus getting back philosophy. The location of the miss matters: long three-point misses carry the ball farther and favour guards and wings, rim misses favour bigs. A team facing a zone gives up different rebounding geometry than against man defence.
stages.distribution: Rebound pool per game is approximately normal around 60 to 70 total opportunities with an sd of about 7, the player's share is a Dirichlet-like split with sd from lineup and positioning.

stages.name: Player rebounding share against teammates and opponents
stages.description: A player's rebound rate (share of available boards while on the floor) depends on size, positioning, effort and opponent size, but it is capped by the competition from teammates on the floor and by the opponent's physical matchup. Rate estimates from 30 games have meaningful sampling error, especially for offensive rebounds which are rare events.
stages.distribution: Rebound rate per minute is stable across seasons for bigs (reliable) and noisy for guards; offensive rebounds approximately Poisson with a mean of about 1 for a rotation big.

stages.name: Assist creation: opportunity times teammate conversion
stages.description: An assist requires a teammate to score after the player's pass. The potential-assist volume depends on the player's share of ball handling and pick-and-roll initiation; conversion depends on teammate shot quality and make rates, which are luck-dominated game by game and shape which shot types (three-pointers and dunks are far more often assisted than isolation twos). When a creator is missing, the other guards' assists rise but with fewer finishers they lose conversion, and when a finisher is missing, the creator's assists fall.
stages.distribution: Assists are overdispersed with variance about 1.4 to 1.8 times the mean; strongly dependent on the number of team made field goals (correlation of about 0.5 between a guard's assists and team makes).

stages.name: Shared game-level shooting shock
stages.description: A single latent factor, how well both teams shoot in this game, enters both stats with opposite signs: more makes mean more assists and fewer rebounds, fewer makes mean more rebounds. This shock is mostly luck, so it is a source of variance and of negative dependence between the two stats for the same player and between players on the same team.
stages.distribution: Shared shock with a loading near +0.6 on assists and about -0.5 on rebounds for guards; the sd of team field-goal percentage in a game is about 7 percentage points.

stages.name: Count distribution, recording and contract
stages.description: The counts are non-negative integers with overdispersion and a mass near zero for low-minute players. The recorded value depends on the official statistician for assists and on team versus individual credit for rebounds. Ladder rungs for a combination stat integrate two correlated counts. Contract details (DNP handling, overtime) are undefined because no series exists.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial for each stat with a negative copula between them; measurement noise of about one unit for assists in a few percent of games.

talent_strength.note: Player rebounding rate and assist creation rate by role; stable for bigs' rebounds and weaker for guards' assists.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent size, scheme and the shot-location mix of misses.

role_personnel.note: Who else is on the floor governs both rebound competition and creation share.

coaching_scheme.note: Crashing the offensive glass versus transition defence, and zone or man schemes, are coaching choices.

environment.note: Altitude and arena conditions change team shooting and pace slightly but have no separate effect on rebound share or assist credit known beyond the pace and scorekeeper terms; none is modelled as its own input.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts truncate starters' minutes; rebounders tend to stay in longer than scorers, so the stat-specific truncation differs.

cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.label: Rebound competition from the other four players on the floor
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.mechanism: A player's rebounds are his share of a pool, and that share falls with the combined rebound rates of lineup partners on the floor.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.rationale: Two good rebounders share one pool; when one is out, the other's rebounds rise by roughly the missing player's share. A per-player rate measured with a different lineup misstates tonight's rate; the effect is largest for bigs.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.measurement: For each lineup scenario k (from availability probabilities), compute share_i,k = r_i / sum_j in lineup(r_j) * team_pool_share, where r is the player's rebound rate per 100 available rebounds estimated from the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+400 minutes) toward position mean; expected rebounds = sum_k P(k) * minutes_i,k/40 * pool_per_40 * share_i,k; separate for offensive (using team ORB%) and defensive boards; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player ORB% and DRB%
raw_data: player ORB% and DRB% by season
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.why: Gives the substitute-and-complement structure that separates rebounds from points, where the pool is not shared.

cbb.miss_location_mix.label: Expected location mix of missed shots (rim, mid-range, three) and perimeter rebound share
cbb.miss_location_mix.mechanism: Long misses from three-point shots produce longer rebounds that go to guards and wings more often, while rim misses go to bigs; a team's shot mix therefore reallocates the rebound pool among positions.
cbb.miss_location_mix.rationale: A guard's rebound line looks high in games where both teams shoot many threes and low against a rim-oriented opponent; position-blind pool totals miss this reallocation.
cbb.miss_location_mix.measurement: For game g, expected misses by zone M_z = sum over both teams of FGA_z * (1 - make_z) using team shot mix and opponent-adjusted zone make rates; perimeter share of rebounds by position from historical play-by-play: P(guard collects | three-point miss) and P(big collects | rim miss) with shrinkage; player-level adjustment: expected rebounds = sum_z M_z * share_player,z shrunk toward the position mean with n/(n+300). As-of: shot mix over the last 15 games.
raw_data: team shot attempts and makes by zone
rebound events with rebounder and shot type
cbb.miss_location_mix.why: Explains why perimeter players' rebounds respond to game shot mix, which the generic pool input does not.

cbb.assist_conversion_chain.label: Assist chain: potential assists times assisted share of teammates' shots
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.mechanism: Expected assists equal the player's share of team creation times the expected number of team assisted field goals, which depends on the mix of shot types (threes and dunks are mostly assisted, post-ups and isolations rarely).
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.rationale: The assist line moves with the team's expected assisted made baskets, a quantity forecastable from shot mix and shot-quality, not from the player's own assist average; scorer discretion adds a venue term.
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.measurement: expected team assisted FGM = sum_z FGA_z * make_z * assisted_share_z (opponent-adjusted, last 15 games with shrinkage n/(n+10)); player assists = creation_share_i (assists per team assisted FGM while on floor, last 2 seasons, shrunk to role mean with n/(n+600 minutes)) * team assisted FGM * (minutes_i/40) * on-floor adjustment for lineup partners; as-of: prior games and scenario weighting.
free_sources: Sports-Reference team and player assist stats
raw_data: team assisted and unassisted FGM by shot type
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.why: Separates the player's creation role from teammates' conversion luck, which the assist-creation entry bundles together.

cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.label: Ball-handler succession: who inherits creation when the primary handler is out
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.mechanism: When a primary creator is absent, assists redistribute to the next handler in a team-specific order and a share of creation is lost because the replacement creates less efficiently.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.rationale: Teammate absence shifts are not symmetric across the roster; some teams have a clear second handler, others spread creation, which changes the sign of the replacement's assist line and the team's total assists.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.measurement: From with/without data over the last two seasons, for each team compute the change in assists per 40 for each rotation player when the primary handler (highest assist share) is off the floor, shrinking with n/(n+250 minutes) to a role-mean redistribution (such as 55 percent to the next guard, 25 percent to wings, 20 percent lost); output the redistribution vector; as-of: prior games.
raw_data: on/off possession and assist data by player
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.why: Defines the successor structure behind an assist prop when a creator is in doubt.

cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.label: Shared game shooting shock with opposite loadings on rebounds and assists
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.mechanism: Game-level team shooting luck raises assists and lowers rebounds; the loading depends on role and is the source of the negative dependence between the two stats.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.rationale: Combination props and parlays need this dependence; ignoring it overstates the variance of rebounds plus assists for guards and misprices both tails of a combined threshold.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.measurement: Estimate a one-factor model on the residuals of rebounds and assists after conditioning on minutes and team pace, with the factor proxy being the standardised team eFG residual in the game; fit loadings lambda_reb and lambda_ast by role (guard, wing, big) over 3 seasons, with shrinkage n/(n+80) to the role pooled loading; simulate stats as NB with means shifted by lambda*z where z ~ N(0,1).
free_sources: Sports-Reference player and team game logs
raw_data: player rebounds and assists per game
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.why: Captures the specific negative dependence between the two stats of this archetype.

cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.label: Offensive-rebounding crash rate versus transition-defence tradeoff by team
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.mechanism: Some coaches send multiple players to the offensive glass, which raises offensive rebounds for the crashers and lowers the opponent's defensive-rebound count, while others retreat to prevent transition scoring.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.rationale: Offensive rebound totals for a big are partly a scheme choice; a high-crash team facing a low-crash opponent offers more rebounds to every big than their per-minute averages from other matchups.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.measurement: For each team compute ORB% (offensive rebounds per available) and opponent transition points per 100 over the last 20 games with half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+10) to the league mean; expected game ORB% for the pair = league mean + 0.5*(crash_A_offense_z + crash_B_defense_allow_z) in standard deviation units of 3.5 points; as-of: prior games.
raw_data: team ORB% and DRB% by game
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.why: Splits offensive from defensive rebounding supply by matchup, which the single pool input blends.

cbb.rebound_pool.reason: Supply of boards is the foundation of the rebound stat; must be built from expected misses of both teams and live free-throw misses, not from team rebounds.

cbb.size_rebounding.reason: Size mismatch moves share but has diminishing effect beyond a threshold gap; partially reflected in rebound rate already.

cbb.assist_creation.reason: Core of the assist prop but bundles creation share and teammate conversion, which need separate treatment.

cbb.player_minutes.reason: Both stats are earned in minutes; blowout truncation affects assists and rebounds differently.

cbb.player_usage.reason: Usage is a scoring concept; for rebounds and assists the relevant rates are rebound share and creation share, so usage is only context for ball-handling role.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Largest controllable shift for both stats (missing big, missing creator); sign depends on the missing player's role.

cbb.defense_style.reason: Zone versus man changes offensive rebound geometry and turnover pressure; effect modest but systematic.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.reason: Opponent allowed rebounds and assists by role are tiny samples and largely reflect pace and team style; keep as heavily shrunk adjustment.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions scale both pools; second order compared with minutes and role.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: Truncates minutes, but for rebounds and assists less than for points because bigs and guards stay in different amounts; needs stat-specific thresholds.

cbb.injuries.reason: Availability of the player and key teammates; the creator versus finisher distinction matters.

cbb.stat_dist.reason: Count shapes and dispersion define every rung, and must include the dependence between the two stats.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path timing is a market diagnostic, not a driver of rebounds or assists.

m.rules_text.reason: No text exists for this archetype; the future rules will define DNP, overtime and statistician sources that determine labels.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook lines are the comparison prior and would hide model edges if used as inputs.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Quote monotonicity across rungs is a market-side check, and the model ladder is monotone by construction.

interactions.mechanism: Rebounds equal the pool per minute times minutes times the player's share, so a game with many misses (slow, poor shooting) multiplies the effect of extra minutes; in a blowout where the pool is the same but minutes drop, the missed-shot supply no longer helps a starter who is sitting.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress player rebounds on expected pool, expected minutes and their product, using starters in prior seasons, and compare to an additive form.

interactions.mechanism: The effect of a teammate's absence on a guard's assists depends on the absent player's role: a missing finisher lowers conversion of the guard's passes and so his assists, while a missing creator hands him more passes; the same input has opposite signs.
interactions.how_to_test: Split with/without games by the absent player's role (creator versus finisher) and compare the change in the guard's assists per 40.

interactions.mechanism: Zone defences keep bigs away from the basket and give up offensive rebounds to the crashing team, so the rebounding advantage of a larger team against a zone is larger than against man defence, in games where the offence is willing to crash.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate offensive rebound percentage in games against zone-heavy opponents versus others, interacted with the team's height and crash tendency.

interactions.mechanism: One shooting shock raises a guard's assists and lowers his rebounds, so a combined threshold has a narrower distribution than independent marginals imply, in the middle, while single-stat tails remain wide; this is a joint distribution feature, not a mean shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the empirical correlation of residual rebounds and assists for guards and compare simulated and observed probabilities of exceeding combined thresholds.

interactions.mechanism: When a co-starting big is out, the other big's rebound share rises by a fraction of the absent player's share, but only if the replacement is smaller; if the replacement is another big the effect is small, and this conditional logic depends on who the replacement is and not only on the absence.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with a missing big, compare rebounds per 40 of the remaining big by replacement type (big versus wing) after controlling for opponent size.

nonlinearities.shape: diminishing returns in the height and weight gap, with saturation beyond about 3 inches per matchup
nonlinearities.why: Share gains from a size advantage flatten once positioning and boxing out are secured, so a linear size-gap term overstates the rebounding of very tall players against average opposition.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in creation share for primary handlers, low and flat for non-handlers
nonlinearities.why: Assists concentrate in the one or two players who start possessions; the step between primary and secondary handler is much larger than the difference in raw passing skill suggests, producing a discontinuity by role.

nonlinearities.shape: stat-specific threshold: minutes cuts start at lower lead margins for guards (assists) than for bigs (rebounds)
nonlinearities.why: Coaches typically pull the guards who run the offence earlier and leave rebounders in to protect the glass, so the high-rung probabilities for assists fall faster with expected margin than those for rebounds.

contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists in the ledger for single-game college three-pointers made, so there is no rules text to read. The intended contract is one named player's three-point field goals made in one game over a half-point or integer threshold, settled from the official box score; the three-point line in men's college basketball is at the international distance, so a made shot counts three points and is recorded as 3PM. What a DNP does to the market, whether overtime counts, and which provider is authoritative are unspecified. The season-long stat-leader series for threes made per game in the unregistered archetype is a different contract and is not evidence for this one.
variants_and_edge_cases: Threes made is a compound count: attempts (a non-negative integer with its own variance) thinned by a make probability, so the zero, one and two-plus rungs have strongly different sensitivities to attempts versus make rate.

Rungs such as '3 or more' sit in the upper tail for most players (a volume shooter attempts about 6 to 8 and makes 35 to 40 percent), where hot-shooting nights dominate and luck is the main determinant.
A player with fewer than five attempts in a blowout or in foul trouble can produce zero even with a good rate; low-minute appearances create a heavy zero mass.
Overtime adds an expected 1 to 2 attempts for a high-volume shooter in the 5 to 6 percent of games that go to extra time; whether those count is undefined.
contract.settlement_data_source: Undefined; official NCAA box score is the likely source. Three-point makes are objective events, so measurement error is smaller than for assists, but late corrections of a made two versus three are possible.

mechanism.summary: Threes made equals the number of three-point attempts times the make probability on each, where attempts are a volume process driven by minutes, role, teammates' ability to create catch-and-shoot looks, opponent scheme and game script (trailing teams shoot more threes), and the make probability is shot-quality and skill, shrunk heavily because college samples of 100 to 200 attempts leave a sampling sd of about 3.5 to 4.5 percentage points, comparable to true differences between shooters. The outcome is therefore a thinned count with uncertainty in both the thinning probability and the attempt rate, so rung probabilities are far more dispersed than a Poisson with the same mean, and edges, if any, come from volume and minutes (forecastable) rather than from make rate (mostly luck).

stages.name: Participation and minutes for the shooter
stages.description: A shooter's expected attempts require him to play, and minutes are a mixture: starters on large favourites are removed in blowouts, and foul trouble reduces minutes in a discrete fashion. Role specialists (spot-up shooters) often play fewer minutes and are more exposed to rotation decisions, so the minute uncertainty has a bigger relative effect on their attempts than for a primary scorer.
stages.distribution: Minutes as a truncated mixture; probability of 20 or fewer minutes for a starter on a favourite can be 20 to 30 percent.

stages.name: Attempt volume from role and the creation of open looks
stages.description: Three-point attempts per minute depend on the player's role (stretch big, spot-up wing, creator), the share of his threes that are assisted catch-and-shoot attempts and thus depend on who creates for him, and the team's scheme. When a primary creator is out, assisted catch-and-shoot threes for the remaining shooters fall, while off-dribble threes rise if the shooter becomes the handler. Pace scales opportunities.
stages.distribution: Attempts per game are overdispersed relative to Poisson (variance about 1.5 times the mean), correlated with minutes and with the number of team possessions.

stages.name: Opponent scheme: volume conceded versus percentage conceded
stages.description: Opponent three-point defence has two parts with very different persistence: the rate of three-point attempts a defence concedes (scheme, zone, pack-line, closeout style) is a persistent trait that changes the shooter's attempts, while the three-point percentage it allows is mostly luck over a season and regresses almost entirely to the mean. A zone that concedes threes raises attempts for spot-up shooters; a pressing, switching defence lowers them.
stages.distribution: Opponent attempts-allowed rate has a season-to-season correlation of about 0.5 to 0.6 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) while percentage allowed has near-zero persistence.

stages.name: Game script: trailing teams shoot more threes
stages.description: Three-point attempts rise when a team is trailing late and falls when it leads comfortably, since the trailing team needs possessions worth three points and the leading team runs the clock. This ties the shooter's attempts to the probability distribution of the game's margin: underdog shooters gain late attempts, favourite shooters lose minutes. The effect interacts with the blowout stage because garbage-time threes are high-volume but low-quality.
stages.distribution: Late-game attempt rate increases by about 15 to 30 percent for the trailing team in the final five minutes (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED magnitude); a small right tail of garbage-time attempts.

stages.name: Make probability: shot quality, skill and heavy regression
stages.description: The probability that an attempt is made depends on shot type (open catch-and-shoot versus contested off-dribble), distance beyond the line, player skill and defender proximity. A single season's percentage is a noisy measure: a 38 percent shooter on 150 attempts has a 95 percent interval of roughly 30 to 46 percent, so the estimate must be a shrunk posterior combining the player's record, the free-throw percentage as a skill proxy and the shot-quality context.
stages.distribution: Posterior Beta distribution for p with an effective prior of about 80 to 120 attempts; game-level Binomial variance adds an sd of about 1.2 makes for six attempts.

stages.name: Compound distribution and ladder mapping
stages.description: The count of makes is the compound of the attempts distribution, the minute mixture and the Beta-uncertain make probability; rung probabilities are read from the compound's cumulative distribution. The zero rung is dominated by low-attempt games, the upper rungs by hot streaks. Contract specifics are unknown, so any rung beyond the first cannot be tied to rules.
stages.distribution: Beta-binomial compound with a negative-binomial attempts mixture and a zero-inflated minute component; overdispersion index of about 1.3 to 1.6 relative to a plain Binomial.

talent_strength.note: Shooting skill with heavy shrinkage and a shot-quality expectation.
