environment.note: Arena conditions (sight lines, backgrounds, altitude) are sometimes cited for shooting but no robust, venue-level effect on three-point percentage separate from the home edge is known, and the shooter's own rate dominates.

cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.label: Expected make probability per three-point attempt from shot context
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.mechanism: The make probability depends on shot type (catch-and-shoot versus off the dribble), defender distance, and distance beyond the arc, so expected conversion can be built before looking at the result.
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.rationale: A shooter on a 44 percent streak from mostly open looks is more likely to regress than the same percentage from contested attempts; the regression target should be quality-implied expectation, not the league mean.
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.measurement: xP = sum_t share_t * (league_make_t shrunk toward the player's make_t with weight n_t/(n_t + 80)) for shot types t in {assisted catch-and-shoot, unassisted off-dribble, transition, corner vs above-the-break}; blend with skill proxy: xP_final = 0.7*xP + 0.3*(0.35 + 0.30*(FT% - 0.72)) using 2-season FT% with n/(n+120) shrinkage; as-of: through prior game; compare to observed 3P% to define a luck residual and regress it by n_attempts.
raw_data: player three-point attempts and makes by assisted flag and zone
league make rates by shot type
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.why: Gives a shot-quality-based target for the three-point make rate so that streaks in 3P% are regressed correctly.

cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.label: Three-point attempt lift when trailing and drop when leading
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.mechanism: The attempt rate for threes rises for a team that is behind and falls for a team that leads late, so a shooter's attempts depend on the distribution of game states his team will occupy.
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.rationale: The underdog's shooter has an additional attempts source late in the game that does not exist for the favourite's shooter, and the distribution of attempts therefore depends on the pregame margin distribution, not only on his season average.
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.measurement: From play-by-play estimate for each team the three-point attempt share of FGA as a function of lead (bins -15 to +15) and time remaining (bins of 5 minutes) over the last 2 seasons, shrunk to the league function with weight n/(n+120 possessions); expected attempts = sum over states of P(state | pregame margin distribution) * attempts_per_possession(state) * possessions in state; as-of: prior games; margin distribution from model not market.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play with score and clock
raw_data: play-by-play shot events with score state and clock
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.why: Connects the shooter's attempts to the pregame margin distribution, a script effect absent from the existing inputs.

cbb.assisted_three_dependency.label: Share of a shooter's threes that are assisted, and by whom
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.mechanism: A spot-up shooter's attempts and quality depend on one or two creators supplying catch-and-shoot passes, so the loss of that creator reduces both attempts and open-look quality.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.rationale: Assisted share varies from about 40 percent for creators to over 90 percent for stationary shooters; teammate absence shifts for creators raise the shooter's off-dribble attempts at lower quality while shooters' catch-and-shoot attempts fall, so the sign depends on dependence.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.measurement: For each shooter compute assisted_share = assisted 3PM / total 3PM and assister distribution over the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+40 makes); with/without effect: delta attempts per 40 and delta make rate when the top assister is off the floor (ridge shrinkage lambda = 150 minutes off); expected scenario shift = sum_k P(creator_k out) * delta_k; as-of: prior games.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.why: Explains how a creator's absence changes a shooter's attempts and quality, beyond a generic teammate-absence shift.

cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.label: Compound distribution of threes made (minutes, attempts, Beta-uncertain make rate)
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.mechanism: Makes are Binomial given attempts and the make probability, attempts are Negative Binomial given minutes, and the make probability has a Beta posterior; marginalising yields the rung probabilities.
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.rationale: A plain Poisson on the mean of makes understates the zero and the upper tails because it ignores uncertainty in attempts and in p; rung pricing at 0.5 and 3.5 requires the compound form.
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.measurement: For each player-game draw minutes from the minute mixture, attempts ~ NB(mean = rate*minutes*pace factor, dispersion fitted from the last 3 seasons by role, typically var = 1.5*mean), p ~ Beta(a0 + makes_prior, b0 + misses_prior) with an effective prior strength of 100 attempts at xP; makes ~ Binomial(attempts, p); compute P(makes >= k) from 20,000 draws or the analytic Beta-Binomial mixture; as-of: pregame.
raw_data: player game logs with 3PA, 3PM and minutes
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.why: Specifies how the rungs of a threes-made ladder are computed from the upstream stages.

cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.label: Opponent three-point defence: persistent attempts conceded versus non-persistent percentage allowed
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.mechanism: A defence's scheme controls the number of threes it concedes, a persistent trait, while the percentage opponents make against it is largely noise.
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.rationale: Opponent allowed 3P% is routinely used as a matchup input but is mostly luck and should be shrunk almost entirely to the league mean, while the attempt-conceded rate retains most of its signal.
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.measurement: att_allowed_z = (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions - league mean)/sd, last 15 games half-life 8 with shrinkage n/(n+10) to prior season value; pct_allowed_z = (opponent 3P% allowed - league)/sd shrunk by weight 0.1 only (set from persistence tests); matchup adjustment to shooter's attempts = 0.6 * att_allowed_z * team-level sd of attempts effect (about 0.8 attempts) and to p = 0.1 * pct_allowed_z * 1.5 points; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik team three-point rate and percentage allowed
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.why: Separates the persistent scheme signal from the non-persistent luck signal in the matchup variable the existing inputs mix.

cbb.player_three_volume.reason: Attempt volume per 40 is the stable and forecastable part of threes made; the entry bundles opponent attempts allowed, which should be separated.

cbb.player_shooting_regression.reason: Make-rate regression is central, but a regression to the league mean ignores shot quality; extended by shot-context expectation.

cbb.player_minutes.reason: Minutes drive attempts; shooters with specialised roles are most exposed to a minutes drop in blowouts.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Generic redistribution; for threes the relevant piece is who creates the assisted looks, which needs the assisted-dependence input.

cbb.defense_style.reason: Zone concedes threes and changes attempts; keep, with measurement through attempts allowed rather than labels.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.reason: Opponent 3P% allowed has almost no persistence, and attempts allowed duplicates defence style; this entry blends them and is mostly noise.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions scale attempts; the effect is proportional and small next to minutes.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: Minute loss for the favourite's shooter is real, but the underdog's shooter gains late attempts, so the sign depends on side.

cbb.three_pt_luck.reason: Team-level three-point luck is the same regression concept at team level; for a player's makes the player-level shrinkage already covers it, and team luck adds only the opponent-quality and teammate-assist channel.

cbb.injuries.reason: Availability of the shooter and the creators; correctly primary given disclosure limits.

cbb.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersed count shape is required, but it must be a compound distribution with uncertainty in p.

m.quote_history.reason: Price movement is market timing information, not a driver of threes.

m.rules_text.reason: Contract definition does not yet exist for threes; the rules when they appear will set the labels.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook three-point lines are the benchmark; using them as an input erases measurable edge.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of quotes is a market-side diagnostic.

interactions.mechanism: Expected attempts equal attempts per minute times minutes, but the variances of the two multiply into an even larger relative spread in attempts for shooters with short and uncertain minutes, so the same average attempts line has fatter tails for rotation shooters than for starters.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare dispersion of attempts per game between starters and bench shooters at equal mean attempts, and test a model with a shared minutes shock.

interactions.mechanism: A zone defence that concedes perimeter looks raises attempts for stationary spot-up shooters more than for creators, who face the same zone with less advantage; the effect of scheme therefore depends on the shooter's role.
interactions.how_to_test: Split shooter games by opponent zone share terciles and by assisted-three share, and compare attempts per 40 changes.

interactions.mechanism: Each additional attempt in the sample adds less weight to the player's own rate in the posterior than the previous one, so the effect of hot streaks on forecast make probability flattens with accumulated attempts; early-season hot shooters are over-weighted if weights are linear in games instead of attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare out-of-sample forecasts for the next 10 games from estimators with shrinkage constant tied to attempts versus tied to games, by attempts to date buckets.

interactions.mechanism: A missing primary creator reduces catch-and-shoot attempts for shooters who depend on that creator's passes and raises off-dribble attempts at lower make rates for shooters who can create for themselves; the sign of the net change in made threes depends on the shooter's assisted share.
interactions.how_to_test: From with/without data, regress the change in made threes per 40 on the shooter's assisted share and the absent creator's assist share.

interactions.mechanism: For a favourite's shooter a blowout means fewer minutes and few late attempts, while for an underdog's shooter the same game means garbage-time attempts at low quality; the game-state regime changes both the volume and the make probability with opposite signs for the two sides.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare threes attempted and made per 40 for the winning and losing team's shooters in games decided by 15 or more points.

nonlinearities.shape: hyperbolic shrinkage weight n/(n+k) in attempts, with k near 80 to 120
nonlinearities.why: Make rate on small samples is almost pure noise and on large samples is informative, so the weight on a player's own percentage rises concavely with attempts; a constant weight misprices early-season hot shooters and freshman shooters.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold-driven mass: P(0 makes) decays roughly geometrically with attempts and jumps for players with fewer than 3 expected attempts
nonlinearities.why: For low-volume shooters the zero rung carries large probability and is sensitive to a one-attempt change in the mean, which is a non-linear region of the cumulative distribution that a normal approximation cannot represent.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating in minutes above about 32 and linear below
nonlinearities.why: Attempts per game plateau for high-volume starters because shot-clock cycles, and plays designed for others, cap the number of attempts, so extra minutes beyond a point add fewer threes than the per-40 rate implies.

contract.settlement_definition: The ledger places 53 outright-futures series under this key: the national champion (KXMARMAD, YES if the named team is the 2026-27 Division 1 National Champion), conference-tournament champions for more than 30 leagues (for example KXNCAAMBIVY and KXNCAAMBHOR, YES if the team is the 2027 conference tournament champion), regular-season conference champions, qualification-for-the-conference-championship-game series (KXNCAAMBBIGEASTQUAL), an NCAA-tournament-round qualification series (KXMARMADROUND, whose sampled text refers to a 'Round of 76') and the NIT. Each is a team-level, season-long event settled by the governing body's results; the sampled text names a season and a competition and does not address vacated results, ineligible teams or the date by which a champion is determined.

rules_evidence.quote: If LSU is the 2026-27 Division 1 Men's College Basketball National Champion, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The national title is a one-winner outright over the 2026-27 season with no stated rule for vacated or revoked titles.

rules_evidence.quote: if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The round series settles on qualification (selection into that round), not on playing, so a withdrawal or forfeit after selection still pays YES.

rules_evidence.quote: qualifies for the Big East conference tournament championship game in the 2026-27 men's college basketball season
rules_evidence.establishes: This is reach-the-final (win two or three games depending on seed and byes), a different event from winning the tournament.

rules_evidence.quote: is the 2027 Men's College Basketball Ivy League conference tournament champion
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference tournament series settle on the champion of that league's postseason tournament, which in the Ivy League is a four-team event.

variants_and_edge_cases: Seven distinct objects share this archetype: the 68-or-more-team national title, a conference tournament championship (30-plus leagues with different formats), a conference regular-season title, reach-the-final, qualify-for-a-named-NCAA-round, NIT winner and the single national-title outright; each has a different path length and a different dependence on bracket seeding.

The sampled round series is named 'Round of 76' and 'qualifies' even if the team 'does not end up competing'; the NCAA field has been 68 teams, so a 76-team format (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) or a Kalshi naming convention changes who counts as qualified, how many play-in games exist and the number of rounds for bubble teams.
Settlement date and vacated results: a title later vacated or an ineligible team are not addressed in any sampled text; for the national title this is a tail risk of order a fraction of a percent.

Multi-day conference tournaments let a top seed with a double bye play fewer games than a lower seed, and in a few leagues the higher seed hosts early rounds, so probability depends on format rather than on rating alone.
Futures are listed months before the field exists: before Selection Sunday the national title probability integrates over whether a team makes the field, its seed and its region.
contract.settlement_data_source: The governing bodies' official results (NCAA for the national championship, each conference for its tournament and standings); the sampled rules name no URL or provider.

mechanism.summary: A title is a product of survival probabilities across a single-elimination bracket whose structure is revealed only on Selection Sunday, and whose team strengths are themselves uncertain months in advance. For the national title, probability equals the chance of reaching the field times the chance of winning six (or seven for play-in teams) neutral-site games, each given by the rating gap through a link with a spread sd of about 10 to 11 points, so small edges compound convexly: a team 3 points better than its competition in each round has a title probability several times that of a team 1 point better. Before the bracket exists the model must integrate over the seed and region assignment, the injury state of stars in March, and the drift of strength between now and then. Conference tournament and regular-season futures run the same logic on a smaller bracket whose format (byes, home hosting, number of rounds) is league-specific and which settles weeks earlier, so one archetype conceals many different path-length structures.

stages.name: Team strength distribution in March, not today
stages.description: A title market opened in November is priced on the strength a team will have in March, which differs from current strength through player development, rotation settling, transfers' integration and injuries; the drift has an sd of several rating points by March for young or churned rosters. The right object is a distribution over March strength, which then goes into the bracket integration, and the spread of that distribution determines how fat the title tail is.
stages.distribution: Random-walk-like innovation in team rating with sd growing as sqrt(time) plus discrete injury jumps; March rating sd about 2 to 3 points of adjusted margin for November pricing, falling to about 1 point by February.

stages.name: Making the field, seed and region
stages.description: Before Selection Sunday a team must earn a place (by conference tournament title or at-large selection), receive a seed (which governs the path and the location), and be placed in a region by committee rules (avoiding same-conference early matchups, proximity placement for top seeds). The format itself may change from year to year: the round naming in the sampled series suggests an expanded field, which changes bid counts and play-in structure. These discrete allocations create jumps in title probability at the moment the bracket is released.
stages.distribution: Discrete seed assignment (1 to 16) with a distribution that is bunched around the rating-implied seed and tilted by resume; region assignment adds a categorical draw affecting path difficulty.

stages.name: Single-game win probability at neutral sites
stages.description: Each tournament game is a neutral-site game (or semi-home for pods), so no home term applies except crowd imbalance in the first weekend when a team plays near campus. The win probability equals the normal CDF of the rating gap over a game sd of about 10 to 11 points, adjusted for pace (slow underdogs shorten the game and add variance), three-point reliance and matchup styles. Empirical seed-based upset rates are a cross-check, not an additional driver, since seeds already encode ratings.
stages.distribution: Win probability as a probit link; the effective sd of margin is larger for three-point-reliant and slow teams; the match-up residual has sd about 2 points of margin per game.

stages.name: Availability and injury shocks across six rounds
stages.description: A single-elimination run lasts three weeks, during which any star's injury or illness changes strength by several points of margin; because a title needs six wins, a team has about six independent chances to be hit by an injury-weakened roster. Disclosure is poor, and an injury during the conference tournament can arrive just before Selection Sunday. The per-game probability of a star missing a game is small but, compounded over a run, is a non-trivial fraction of title equity for top teams.
stages.distribution: Mixture over player availability states with a per-game miss probability near 2 to 4 percent for each top-three player; correlated within a team through shared load and travel.

stages.name: Conference-level tournaments and regular-season races
stages.description: More than thirty series settle on a conference tournament title, reach-the-final or regular-season championship. These follow the same win-probability logic on a small bracket whose format is league-specific: some leagues give the top seeds double byes, some play at campus sites, some are four-team events like the Ivy tournament. Path length (two to five games) and home hosting change title equity of the top seed far more than rating gaps do, and the winner of a one-bid league gets the automatic NCAA bid, which shapes motivation for bubble teams.
stages.distribution: Short single-elimination or double-bye brackets with 3 to 5 games; title probability for the top seed typically between 25 and 45 percent in 10-to-14-team leagues, and higher with byes.

stages.name: Contract mapping: title, finals, qualification
stages.description: The same simulated paths settle different contracts: win-all-six for the title, win-k-games for reach-the-final or round qualification, and rank-based conditions for regular-season titles. Qualification pays even if the team does not compete, so only selection matters for that series. The simulation must keep joint structure (two teams in the same half cannot both reach the final), which matters for parlays and for the sum of probabilities across teams equalling one.
stages.distribution: Paths are exchangeable only after conditioning on the bracket; the sum over teams of title probabilities is exactly 1, and uncertainty in strength induces positive correlation among a team's own round probabilities.

game_context_script.note: Game-level variance by style (tempo and three-point reliance) is the only script-level effect used for a season-long future.

pace_volume.note: Pace matters through the game's margin variance (slow underdogs), not through a separate volume term.

efficiency_conversion.note: Efficiency enters through the rating; a luck regression of recent shooting is inside the ratings pipeline and not a separate input.

distribution_variance.note: Fat title tails come from strength uncertainty compounded over six rounds; correlations among a team's round outcomes are induced by the shared strength draw.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Format, byes and multi-day fatigue in conference tournaments; stakes for auto-bid teams.

cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.label: Distribution of team strength change from pricing date to Selection Sunday
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.mechanism: Team strength evolves through development, rotation settling, transfer integration and injuries; the change from a given date to March is a random variable with a team-type-dependent sd.
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.rationale: A November title probability is an expectation over March strength; using today's rating as if it were March's understates tail teams and overstates favourites, and the correct sd depends on roster continuity and age.
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.measurement: For each past season and each date d (weekly), compute delta = rating_March (final pre-tournament adjusted margin) - rating_d for each team; regress delta on rating_d (mean reversion), games_played_d, returning minutes share, roster age (minutes-weighted class year), and injury indicator; model delta ~ N(b*(rating_d - league_mean), sd_d) with sd_d = sqrt(a^2 + c^2*(games_remaining/30)) fitted on at least 12 seasons; output the posterior over March rating by team; as-of: rating snapshot date.
raw_data: team rating by date for each season
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.why: Converts a snapshot rating into the March strength distribution that title odds actually depend on.

cbb.pod_site_proximity.label: Distance from campus to first- and second-round site and expected crowd imbalance
cbb.pod_site_proximity.mechanism: The NCAA places pods across the country and seeds are matched to sites by geography, so some teams play 50 miles from home and others 2,000, with corresponding crowd and travel effects.
cbb.pod_site_proximity.rationale: A near-home team in rounds 1 and 2 gets a semi-home margin bonus of one to three points relative to a neutral model, and a distant 2-seed may be at a relative disadvantage; the effect compounds through two rounds of the path.
cbb.pod_site_proximity.measurement: For each team-seed-site combination compute great-circle distance campus to arena in miles, a binary indicator for within 250 miles, and an attendance-share proxy (school's average road attendance rank); margin adjustment = b1*I(<250 mi) + b2*log(distance) fitted on 20 tournaments of game margins vs rating-implied margins (expected b1 about 1.5 to 2.5 points, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); applied only to rounds 1 and 2 (and regional sites if close); as-of: bracket release.
free_sources: Sports-Reference tournament game results with sites
cbb.pod_site_proximity.why: Adds a path-specific environment term to title odds for first-weekend games.

cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.label: Conference tournament format table for 2026-27 (size, byes, hosting, seeding, tiebreakers)
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.mechanism: Each league has its own bracket: number of participants, byes for top seeds, campus versus neutral venue, reseeding, tiebreakers that set seeds, and days of rest between games.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.rationale: More than thirty ledger series settle on a conference tournament; probability for the top seed varies by format as much as by rating (a top seed with a double bye needs three wins in a 14-team field, a four-team Ivy field needs two), and some formats let the higher seed host.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.measurement: Maintain a table with fields: league, teams in field, rounds, byes by seed, hosting rule (neutral, campus, higher-seed), venue city, dates, tiebreaker order for regular-season seeding, auto-bid flag; simulate the league bracket from the current standings projection using the model's pairwise win probability with a home adjustment of 3.5 points where the format hosts; refresh when conferences announce changes (realignment, new members) before each season; as-of: announcement date.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.why: Defines the path-length structure of 30-plus ledger series that the generic bracket simulation input does not specify.

cbb.two_way_balance_profile.label: Two-way balance profile: joint offence and defence rank at the top of the rating list
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.mechanism: Champions in the efficiency era have mostly been ranked highly in both offence and defence; a team strong on only one side may have a different tournament win probability than its net rating suggests because of matchup variance.
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.rationale: This is a hypothesis from historical regularities, not an established causal driver; it is included as a testable signal because it could capture shot-making variance in single games (offence-dependent teams have wider outcomes).
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.measurement: Compute min(off_rank, def_rank) and the absolute difference |off_rank - def_rank| in the final pre-tournament snapshot; flag balanced if both top 25 or the minimum rank 20 or better; test in historical tournaments whether the residual of advancement versus rating-implied probability (probit) is explained by the balance flag after controlling for net rating (a likelihood-ratio test across at least 20 tournaments); as-of: Selection Sunday snapshot.
raw_data: pre-tournament offence and defence ranks by team per season
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.why: Gives a specific, falsifiable top-end filter for title futures without assuming it is real.

cbb.tournament_field_format.label: NCAA tournament field structure and seeding rules for 2027
cbb.tournament_field_format.mechanism: The number of teams, play-in games, at-large and automatic bids, seeding S-curve and region placement rules define which paths exist and how many rounds each team must win.
cbb.tournament_field_format.rationale: The sampled round series refers to a 'Round of 76', which implies a field larger than the 68-team format; this changes bubble probabilities, the number of games for the lowest seeds and the title path for play-in teams, so any title model built on the 68-team structure may be wrong.
cbb.tournament_field_format.measurement: Record for the season: field size, number of first-round or play-in games, number of automatic and at-large bids, rounds required for each seed line, S-curve rules, bracket-integrity rules (conference avoidance until a specified round) and effective dates; simulate seed to path accordingly; as-of: NCAA announcement date; verify against NCAA.com before each season.
raw_data: field size and bid counts by season
cbb.tournament_field_format.why: Settlement-critical structural input for both title and qualification series.

cbb.bracket_sim.reason: Mislabelled as a team-strength input: it is the integrator (a model) that turns ratings and structure into title odds, so it needs to be audited as a method with explicit seed and region uncertainty.

cbb.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability-adjusted strength matters mainly through star injury risk in March; before the bracket it is a modest adjustment.

cbb.title_path.reason: Path and region strength are outputs of the bracket simulation for a given draw, not an independent input; listing both double counts the same mechanism.

cbb.single_game_variance.reason: Style-dependent game variance fattens the title tail; the magnitude is modest next to rating uncertainty and is hard to measure.

cbb.seed_upset_priors.reason: Seeds already encode ratings, so historical upset rates by seed double count strength; useful as a calibration target for the simulator, not as an input.

cbb.star_injury_risk.reason: Compounded over six rounds it is a real component of title equity; disclosure and base rates are limited.

cbb.in_season_improvement.reason: Part of the trajectory term; better replaced by the explicit March-strength distribution.

cbb.recruit_exp.reason: Experience and recruiting add little once an efficiency rating exists; the evidence for an independent tournament experience effect is thin.

cbb.popularity_bias.reason: Brand-driven price bias is a feature of the market price, not of the outcome; it belongs to calibration of the benchmark.

interactions.mechanism: Title probability is a product over six games of win probabilities that are probit in rating gap over game sd, so the log-title probability is approximately linear in rating gap and its sensitivity to game sd is largest for the favourite: a modest increase in game variance transfers a large share of title equity from the best team to the field.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the field with sd 9, 10.5 and 12 and compare the shift in the top team's title probability, then check historical top-seed title frequency against the sd that matches it.

interactions.mechanism: Title and qualification probabilities for a bubble or low-seed team depend on the field size and play-in structure: in an expanded field an extra play-in win may be required for the lowest seeds, and the allocation of bids changes who is in at all, so the simulator output is conditional on the format.
interactions.how_to_test: Run the bracket simulator under 68-team and 76-team structures with identical ratings and compare title and qualification probabilities for teams ranked 40 to 80.

interactions.mechanism: The loss of one top player cuts strength by an amount that depends on the replacement and the team's depth; combined with the number of rounds (each with an independent miss probability) the strength distribution of a title contender is a mixture whose lower component holds nontrivial weight, and the favourite's title probability is the weighted sum over states.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute title probability for a top team under a no-injury state and under a star-out state and mix with per-game miss probabilities; compare to a model that uses average strength.

interactions.mechanism: A top seed with a double bye plays one fewer game and has an extra rest day, while a lower seed must win four games in four days; the advantage of a bye grows with the length of the bracket and with how thin the team's rotation is, so the fatigue effect depends on the format.
interactions.how_to_test: Using past conference tournaments compare win rates of seeds by number of games needed and rotation depth after controlling for rating.

interactions.mechanism: Because title probability is convex in strength, adding uncertainty about March strength raises the title probability of mid-tier contenders and lowers the favourite's (Jensen's inequality on the exponential-like tail), so the same current rating gap yields different odds in November and in February.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute title odds of the same team with sd 0, 1.5 and 3 for March rating and compare with the historical frequency by preseason rank.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential-like convexity of title probability in rating gap (product of six probit terms)
nonlinearities.why: A one point rating edge raises each round's win probability by about 3 percentage points near 50 percent, which compounds into a title probability that rises several-fold; a linear model on rating cannot reproduce the tail concentration at the top.

nonlinearities.shape: variance grows with horizon (sqrt time) and the mean reverts toward the league mean
nonlinearities.why: A November rating overstates how far a team will stand from average in March, so the best and worst teams revert; the sd of change is larger for new rosters, making the horizon effect conditional on roster continuity.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating effect on title probability beyond a game sd of about 12 points
nonlinearities.why: Once the game sd is already large, additional variance shifts title equity from the favourite to the field by progressively less, since probabilities approach a floor determined by bracket structure.

contract.settlement_definition: The ledger puts 16 team-season series here: regular-season conference finish thresholds (KXNCAAMBACCREGTOP and the Big Ten, Big East, Big 12, SEC and Big 10 variants, 'top 4' with every tied team counted as achieving the position), regular-season win totals (KXNCAAMBWINS, floor_strike 30), undefeated seasons (KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATED) and undefeated at home excluding neutral sites (KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATEDHOME), two teams both reaching the Round of 16 (KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL) and several March Madness seed series (KXMARMADSEED, 1SEED, HIGHSEED, SEEDSUM, SEEDWIN) that are title only. Regular-season series count only official regular-season games and exclude conference-tournament and postseason games; the tournament-based series settle on the NCAA tournament result.

rules_evidence.quote: all tied teams will resolve as having achieved that position
rules_evidence.establishes: Top-N finishes use a tie-inclusive rule on conference win-loss records: no tiebreaker is applied, so every team tied at the cutoff pays YES and the probabilities across teams can sum to more than N.

rules_evidence.quote: Any conference tournament or postseason tournament games do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Win totals are counted over the regular season only, so conference-tournament and NCAA games add nothing to the count.

rules_evidence.quote: Neutral site games do not count as a home game for either team.
rules_evidence.establishes: The home-only undefeated series counts only games at the team's official home arena, so exempt events and neutral-site non-conference games are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: both qualify for the Round of 16 in the 2027 men's college basketball tournament
rules_evidence.establishes: A conjunction of two teams' advancement to the Round of 16 (Sweet 16 in NCAA terms), requiring that they do not eliminate each other earlier.

rules_evidence.quote: This market only considers regular season games as defined by the league's governing body.
rules_evidence.establishes: The undefeated season ignores postseason play, and the definition of a regular-season game is the governing body's, not the market's.

variants_and_edge_cases: Top-N finish series (ACC, Big Ten, Big East, Big 12, SEC) use inclusive ties on conference win-loss records: if three teams tie for 4th, all three resolve YES, so the standings model must compute 'wins at least the N-th best total' rather than rank after tiebreakers.

Win totals count official regular-season games only; whether games against non-Division I opponents, exempt events and games played in an in-season tournament count as official, and how many games the team plays (27 to 31), is not stated, and strikes such as 30 wins need near-perfection.
Undefeated at home excludes neutral-site games and conference-tournament games, so only conference and non-conference games in the team's own arena count; the number of home games is 14 to 17.

KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL (two named teams both reaching the Round of 16) is a joint advancement event whose probability depends on whether the two can meet before that round, on shared region placement and on the committee's same-conference avoidance rules.
Seed series (KXMARMADSEED, 1SEED, HIGHSEED, SEEDSUM, SEEDWIN) are title only: their definitions (for example which seed wins the title, the sum of seeds of the Final Four) are not visible.
contract.settlement_data_source: Conference and NCAA official standings and records for regular-season series; NCAA tournament official results for Round-of-16 series; the rules name 'the league's governing body' but no specific URL.

mechanism.summary: These contracts are functions of a team's whole season of games, so the key quantity is not a per-game probability but the joint distribution over a season of outcomes driven by a shared latent strength. Undefeated and high win-total events are tails of a Poisson-binomial whose per-game win probabilities are positively correlated through that shared strength, so P(30-0) is far above the product of marginals evaluated at the mean strength. Top-N conference finishes are order statistics of the conference win totals of all teams, with tie-inclusive settlement, on unbalanced schedules in which some opponents are played once and some twice and venue alternates. The tournament-related members (both teams to the Round of 16, seed series) add a bracket stage whose structure is revealed only on Selection Sunday and whose dependence between two teams comes from shared regions and avoidance rules.

stages.name: Season-long strength as a shared latent variable
stages.description: A team's per-game win probabilities across a 30-game season are tied together by the same underlying strength, which is uncertain at the time of pricing; if the team is better than its rating, many games are easier than priced, if worse, many are harder. The uncertainty is larger for rosters with heavy transfer turnover and shrinks as the season progresses, but never to zero. This shared factor is what makes undefeated and 30-win events far likelier than independence implies.
stages.distribution: Normal posterior on team strength with sd about 2 to 3 points of adjusted margin early in the season, decaying with games played; the shared factor induces a game-to-game correlation of about 0.05 to 0.15 in outcomes.

stages.name: Which games exist and which count
stages.description: The number of games, their sites and opponents define the event space: a 31-game schedule with exempt events, neutral-site tournaments, buy games at home and conference play of 18 to 20 games, with new alignments making the conference schedule unbalanced (some opponents once, some twice). Official counting rules (exempt events, games against non-D1 teams, the postseason exclusion) decide which games enter a win total or an undefeated count.
stages.distribution: Fixed discrete schedule with known opponents but uncertain eligibility rules; home games 14 to 17, neutral games 2 to 5, conference games 18 to 20.

stages.name: Game-level win probabilities with venue and availability
stages.description: Each game's win probability comes from the strength gap plus a venue shift (home, away or neutral), rest and a minutes-weighted availability adjustment for known absences. Over a season roughly a third of the games are away games in which a strong team's win probability drops by 10 to 15 percentage points, so undefeated probabilities hinge on the few road games against good conference opponents.
stages.distribution: Probit link with game sd near 10.5 points; per-game win probability ranges from 5 percent (road at a top opponent) to over 99 percent (home buy game).

stages.name: Season totals: Poisson-binomial with shared strength
stages.description: Given the game probabilities and the shared strength draw, the win total is a sum of correlated Bernoulli outcomes; the distribution of total wins is therefore overdispersed relative to a Poisson-binomial with fixed probabilities, with fatter tails at both ends. Undefeated is the extreme tail of the same distribution, and the home-only undefeated variant uses only the home subset and has a different (smaller but easier) set of games.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed Poisson-binomial; variance of the season win total inflated by roughly 20 to 40 percent relative to independence when strength sd is 2 to 3 points; undefeated probability is the product of conditional probabilities integrated over the strength draw.

stages.name: Conference order statistics with tie-inclusive cutoffs
stages.description: A top-N conference finish is determined by the N-th highest conference win total among all teams, and each team that ties at or above that number counts. The probability for team i depends on the joint distribution of all teams' win totals with strong dependence (when one team wins, another loses within the conference), so independent per-team models fail; tiebreakers, used for tournament seeding, are not used for this settlement.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution of conference win totals with a zero-sum constraint (conference wins equal conference losses overall); tie mass at the cutoff is typically 15 to 35 percent in 14 to 18 team leagues.

stages.name: Postseason link: joint advancement and seed lines
stages.description: Round-of-16 conjunctions and seed series are decided in March after the bracket is released. For two named teams the joint probability depends on whether they can meet before the Round of 16 (the committee avoids same-conference matchups early), whether they land in the same region, and the shared dependence on seeds and pods. Seed-line series depend on committee behaviour at the boundaries.
stages.distribution: Joint advancement of two teams: approximately the product of marginals when in separate regions, lower when they can meet in the second round and zero if they are paired against one another.

talent_strength.note: Shared latent strength with uncertainty is the foundation for season-long events.

opponent_matchup.note: Game-level matchup variance and the bracket structure for the postseason-linked series.

role_personnel.note: Availability-adjusted rating captures who plays, but roster role detail is secondary for season-long events.

availability_news.note: Injuries enter through the strength posterior and game-level adjustment; a long absence of a star changes the shared factor for the rest of the season.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching effects on season win totals and conference finish are captured by team ratings and no separate coach-level driver of schedule-level outcomes beyond rating is established; effects on end-of-season rest are covered by the clinch input.

environment.note: Home, away and neutral allocation of the schedule is central to undefeated and home-only series.

game_context_script.note: In-game script (blowouts, foul games) changes margins but not whether a team wins or loses, which is what these season-level contracts count; script matters only for spread-like contracts.

pace_volume.note: Possession count affects margin variance within a game, which is reflected in the single-game sd; it is not a separate driver of season win counts or finish ranks.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency luck matters within the ratings pipeline and the shared strength posterior; a separate efficiency input for season-level counts would double count the rating uncertainty.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed season totals and zero-sum conference win totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and incentives for teams that clinched or are eliminated late in the season.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating crews rotate across games and teams over a season, so no team-specific crew effect can change a season-long win total beyond what home-court and ratings already capture.

settlement_contract.note: Tie-inclusive top-N, regular-season-only counts and neutral-site exclusion are all explicit; non-D1 and exempt-event counting remains ambiguous.

cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.label: Tie-inclusive top-N cutoff probability from the joint conference win-total distribution
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.mechanism: A team finishes in the top N if its conference wins are at least the N-th highest total among all teams, with every tied team counting.
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.rationale: Standings simulations that apply conference tiebreakers produce a rank, but the contract ignores tiebreakers and pays all tied teams; using tiebreaker ranks understates probabilities near the cutoff and makes team probabilities sum to exactly N when the contract's sum exceeds N.
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.measurement: Simulate the conference season 20,000 times: draw each team's strength from its posterior, draw every remaining conference game with home-adjusted probit probability, tally conference wins; for each simulation compute W_N = N-th largest win total; team i hits if W_i >= W_N; probability = hit frequency; report the expected number of teams hitting (greater than N); as-of: standings and ratings snapshot with remaining games.
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.why: Aligns the standings model with the contract's tie rule, which the existing tiebreaker-based standings simulation does not.

cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.label: Shared-strength correlation among a team's game outcomes
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.mechanism: Because one latent strength governs all of a team's games, outcomes are positively correlated; the Poisson-binomial with independent games understates tails.
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.rationale: Undefeated and 30-win series sit in the extreme upper tail, where integrating over strength uncertainty increases the probability by large factors relative to plugging in the mean; the same shared factor raises the variance of every win total.
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.measurement: Draw s_i ~ N(rating_i, sd_t) with sd_t = sqrt(a^2 + b*(games_remaining/30)) calibrated so that the realised distribution of final win totals matches history (a ~ 1.5 points, b ~ 4 for new rosters); condition each game's probability on s_i and s_j; compute P(all wins) = E_s[prod_g p_g(s)] by Monte Carlo (20,000 draws); calibrate sd_t on 15 prior seasons by checking coverage of final win totals (probability integral transform uniformity); as-of: rating snapshot.
free_sources: Bart Torvik / Sports-Reference historical ratings and results
raw_data: historical preseason and in-season ratings with final records
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.why: Specifies how season-long tails are generated; the existing ratings and rating uncertainty inputs are not linked to season totals.

cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.label: Regular-season game inventory: number of games, sites, opponent class and which count as official
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.mechanism: The event space for win totals, undefeated and home-only series is the list of games that count, which depends on exempt events, non-D1 opponents, neutral sites and the league's definition.
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.rationale: A 30-win strike on a team that plays 29 counted games is impossible, and one that plays 31 allows a loss; the home-only series has between 14 and 17 games and excludes all neutral-site games; each ambiguity changes the probability by a large factor.
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.measurement: Per team and season record: scheduled games (date, opponent, site type home/away/neutral, event name, D1 flag, counts toward official record flag, conference flag) from the school and NCAA schedule; total counted games N, home counted games H; probability tables computed over counted games only; refresh when the schedule changes (cancellations, added games); as-of: schedule snapshot date.
raw_data: team schedules with site type and event labels
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.why: Defines which games the contract counts and how many exist, a settlement-critical input absent from the existing list.

cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.label: Dependence of two teams' tournament advancement (region, pod, avoidance rules)
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.mechanism: Two teams' advancement probabilities are linked through the bracket: they cannot both advance if they meet, and share region and pod strength.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.rationale: KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL asks for both teams in the Round of 16; the committee generally avoids same-conference matchups before the third round for teams of the same conference, but region and pod placement still matter and a correlation from correlated rating uncertainty exists.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.measurement: Simulate the bracket 50,000 times from the seed and region distribution (before Selection Sunday) or from the actual bracket (after): P(both reach R16) = joint frequency; also report the independence benchmark P_A*P_B and the ratio; the committee rule used is: same-conference teams avoided in rounds 1 and 2 where possible (verify yearly with the NCAA's principles and procedures document); as-of: bracket release.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.why: Gives the joint probability for conjunction contracts, which the marginal-only bracket simulation does not output.

cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.label: Effort and rotation change after clinching or elimination from title races
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.mechanism: Teams that have clinched a seed or title, or are out of any race, may rest starters or alter intensity in the last games, which shifts win probabilities against the pure strength gap.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.rationale: Top-N and win-total contracts include the last two weeks of the conference season in which stakes differ across teams; an incentive-blind model overstates the win probability of clinched teams and understates that of teams chasing a bid or a top-four double bye.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.measurement: Define stakes_i,g = |dP(top4 finish)/d(win this game)| from the standings simulation and the bubble/seed leverage from the resume model; regress game margin residuals (actual minus rating-implied) on stakes_i - stakes_j and a clinch flag using 8 seasons of the final 6 conference games; expected effect 0.5 to 1.5 points (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); as-of: standings before each game.
raw_data: seed and bid leverage computed by simulation
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.why: A measurable replacement for the generic motivation label in the existing list, specific to season-ending leverage.

cbb.ratings.reason: Needs to be a posterior over season-long strength with uncertainty and correlation across games; a point rating gives wrong tails for undefeated and win totals.

cbb.conference_standings_sim.reason: Core model for finish-based series, but applies conference tiebreakers that the sampled top-N rules do not use (all tied teams count), so it needs the tie-inclusive cutoff variant.

cbb.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining schedule strength is an implicit output of the standings simulation, which uses the actual remaining games; as a stand-alone feature it duplicates the simulation.

cbb.bracket_sim.reason: Required only for the Round-of-16 and seed series in this archetype; irrelevant for regular-season finish, wins and undefeated contracts.

cbb.conf_tourney_fatigue.reason: Relevant to conference-tournament series (ledgered under the champion archetype) but none of the sampled regular-season or undefeated series depend on it.

cbb.venue.reason: Home, away and neutral allocation of the schedule drives undefeated and home-only probabilities; modest as a single-game shift but central in aggregation.

cbb.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability enters season totals mainly through long absences; for a single game it is small relative to strength uncertainty.

cbb.auto_bid_structure.reason: Auto-bid structure matters for bid-thief and bubble questions rather than for the sampled regular-season or undefeated series.

cbb.motivation.reason: Generic stakes label without a measurement; replaced by leverage computed from the standings simulation.

cbb.single_game_variance.reason: Style-specific variance changes individual game win probabilities and upset tails; its effect on season totals is modest.

m.quote_history.reason: Shows how market prices respond to results and injuries over a long season; not a determinant of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Tie-inclusive finish rule, neutral-site exclusion and regular-season-only counts are the contract's decisive details.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook season win totals and futures are the benchmark; they carry vig and must not be fed back as inputs.

m.ladder_structure.reason: For win totals the cross-strike monotonicity (for example 28, 29 and 30 wins) is a market-side check, and the model ladder is monotone by construction.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of an undefeated season is the expectation over strength of a product of per-game win probabilities, which is convex in strength; adding uncertainty therefore raises the probability substantially for strong teams (for example from 1 percent at fixed strength to 3 percent), and the proportional lift grows with the number of games.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(undefeated) for the top-5 rated teams with strength sd of 0, 1.5 and 3 and compare against historical frequency of unbeaten starts after 10 games.

interactions.mechanism: Probability of a top-4 finish depends on the distribution of the fourth-best win total in the whole league, which changes with how many strong teams there are; the same team has a lower probability in a league with six contenders than in one with four, and the tie-inclusive rule raises it most when the cutoff is crowded.
interactions.how_to_test: Evaluate the same team's top-4 probability across simulated league compositions and compare tie-inclusive and tiebreaker-based ranks.

interactions.mechanism: The home-only undefeated contract uses only home games (14 to 17), each with a high win probability, so the probability is dominated by the weakest home opponents and by the number of conference home games against top teams; the full-season undefeated contract adds roughly half as many road and neutral games with much lower probabilities, giving different regimes for the two contracts.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the product of home-game probabilities and of all-game probabilities for the same teams and compare against historical frequencies of home-unbeaten and fully unbeaten seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Effort changes appear only after a team's stakes cross a threshold: a team that clinched the top seed loses incentive and may rest starters in the final games, while a team one win away from a double bye does not; the effect is a function of leverage computed from the standings simulation.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare late-season margin residuals for teams with clinched status versus similar teams with high leverage, using the simulation-based leverage measure.

interactions.mechanism: For two teams of the same conference, advancement is jointly shaped by committee avoidance rules and by whether both are in the field at all (a one-bid league cannot supply two teams); the joint probability depends on the seed assignment of both and on the conference's bid count.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the pair's joint advancement with and without the same-conference avoidance rule and compare to the product of marginals.

nonlinearities.shape: convex mapping from team strength to P(undefeated) and P(30+ wins), roughly exponential in strength
nonlinearities.why: A product of many win probabilities near 0.9 to 0.99 is extremely sensitive to the average per-game probability: one point of rating changes P(undefeated) by roughly 30 to 40 percent proportionally, so tails need the full strength posterior.

nonlinearities.shape: step difference between home and road win probabilities of about 10 to 15 percentage points for favourites
nonlinearities.why: Aggregation of a few road or neutral games near 70 to 80 percent dominates the failure probability of an undefeated season, so the venue effect enters the product as discrete downgrades rather than a smooth shift.

nonlinearities.shape: cutoff crowding effect: top-N probability rises with tie mass at the cutoff
nonlinearities.why: Because tied teams all count, the effective probability of a team at the margin of the top four increases non-linearly with the share of simulations in which three or more teams tie at the fourth-place win total.

contract.settlement_definition: No ledger series is attached to this key, so there is no rules text for seed-line, made-the-field, round-reached or other team futures under it. The intended contract is a team-level statement about the NCAA tournament's selection and bracket: the seed line the committee assigns, whether the team is in the field (automatic or at-large bid), the round it reaches, or similar. Such markets would settle on the NCAA's official bracket and results. The five March Madness seed series that exist on Kalshi (seed, seed win, seed sum, number of one seeds, high seed) are ledgered under the conference-futures archetype and are title only, so their exact definitions cannot be assumed here.
variants_and_edge_cases: Seed-line contracts depend on the committee's S-curve and its bracketing constraints: a team ranked 8th among the top-seeded group can be moved a line to avoid same-conference matchups, so the seed line is not a deterministic function of rank.

Made-the-field contracts include automatic bids (conference tournament champions) and at-large bids; whether a team that qualifies but is later ineligible or withdraws counts is a settlement question (the round-qualification series sampled elsewhere pays even if the team does not compete).

A play-in or First Four team and a 16 seed are both low seeds with different path lengths; if the 2027 field is expanded beyond 68 teams (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), the number of play-in games and which seeds play them changes round-reached definitions.

Round-reached contracts for a given round are nested events (reach round 2 includes reach round 3), so a ladder of strikes must have monotone probabilities and may be influenced by whether the play-in round counts as a round.
contract.settlement_data_source: NCAA official selection show bracket and tournament results (NCAA.com); no rules text exists to confirm.

mechanism.summary: The seed and field are produced by a human committee applying published principles to a set of metrics, so the generating process is a noisy ordinal ranking, not a game outcome. The committee builds a team sheet from result-based measures (NET's team value, quadrant records, wins above bubble, strength of record) and predictive ratings, ranks all candidates, and then fits them into an S-curve with bracketing constraints. The probability a team makes the field is the probability its committee rank lies inside the at-large cutoff after bid thieves (automatic-bid winners who would not have been at-large) are removed; the probability of a given seed line is the probability its slot falls inside a four-slot band after constraint moves. Late results, conference tournaments and committee judgement on injuries and recency add noise, so probabilities near boundaries are sensitive and the entire distribution is step-like (ordinal) rather than smooth. Round-reached outcomes then follow from the bracket simulation conditional on the assigned seed.

stages.name: Resume at Selection Sunday: results, quality and strength
stages.description: Each team accumulates a resume over the season: the quality of wins and losses (quadrants determined by opponent rank and site), strength of schedule, wins above a bubble team and predictive efficiency. How the final resume looks depends on the remaining games, which differ in leverage: a win over a top-30 opponent on the road adds much more than a home win over a 250th-ranked team, while a loss to a Q3 or Q4 team costs heavily.
stages.distribution: Resume metrics are ordinal or bounded: quadrant counts are integers, WAB is approximately normal with sd of about 1 win by February, NET rank changes by 2 to 6 positions per game for bubble teams.

stages.name: Committee ranking as revealed preference with noise
stages.description: The committee does not apply a formula: it weighs NET, quadrant records, predictive metrics and its own judgement, and the weighting shifts between the top of the field, where quality wins and predictive rating matter more, and the bubble, where record against the quadrants dominates. A fitted ordered-probit on past seeds estimates the weights and the committee noise, which is of the order of two to four seed slots at the boundaries. Recent results may weigh more than early-season ones.
stages.distribution: Ordered-probit style latent score with committee noise sd about 2 to 4 rank slots; metric weights differ across seed ranges.

stages.name: Automatic bids and bid thieves
stages.description: Each of the roughly 30 conferences sends its tournament champion automatically. When a champion would not have been selected at-large (a bid thief), the number of at-large slots available to bubble teams falls by one. The count of thieves is random and depends on the conference tournaments of multi-bid leagues; a 3-bid league that loses its favourite in the tournament can produce a thief. This count shifts the cutoff by several slots.
stages.distribution: The number of bid thieves is approximately Poisson-binomial with mean 1 to 3 per year; each additional thief moves the effective at-large cutoff by one slot.

stages.name: Availability and committee treatment of injuries
stages.description: A team missing a key player at Selection Sunday may be seeded as a team that would play without him (committee principles mention availability) or as it was over the season, with unclear weighting. Because disclosure is thin, the market and the model may disagree on whether a star will be back, and an injury in the conference tournament changes the committee's view without changing any metric much.
stages.distribution: Binary-like treatment effect on seed with magnitude of 0 to 2 lines for key players out; uncertain sign convention across years.

stages.name: S-curve placement and bracketing constraints
stages.description: After ranking, teams are placed on the S-curve in seed lines of four, then adjusted to satisfy rules: no same-conference matchups before a stated round where avoidable, balanced regions, proximity placements for top seeds and pod site assignments. These adjustments can move a team one seed line away from its rank-implied line, and the effect is a discrete jump in seed distribution.
stages.distribution: Discrete seed-line assignment with a most likely value and neighbours at 15 to 30 percent probability each for teams near line boundaries.

stages.name: Advancement after seeding
stages.description: Once the bracket is set, round-reached outcomes are determined by single-game win probabilities along the path, with seed-specific historical base rates as a calibration target. A team's seed and region decide the opponents; upsets are driven by game variance and stylistic matchups.
stages.distribution: Nested advancement events with monotone probabilities; round-reached distribution is convex in rating gap and path strength.

talent_strength.note: Resume and predictive metrics plus the committee's revealed weights.

opponent_matchup.note: Path structure for round-reached; seeds feed matchups.

role_personnel.note: The selection of a team depends on its season results and rating, not on role-level lineup composition; role enters only through availability (covered separately) and the strength rating itself.

availability_news.note: Committee treatment of injured stars and communications of status at Selection Sunday.

coaching_scheme.note: The relevant coaching-like layer is the committee's behaviour (chair, members, protocol), not team coaches.

environment.note: Seeding does not depend on venue conditions beyond their effect on the results already in the resume; site assignments of pods are a bracket output, covered in the champion archetype's proximity input.

game_context_script.note: In-game script has no role in committee selection other than through final scores in NET margin components (capped), which are already inside the resume metrics.

pace_volume.note: Possession counts are not a driver of selection or seed lines; tempo affects only game variance, which is addressed in advancement.

efficiency_conversion.note: Net efficiency is a component of NET and of the predictive ratings the committee consults.

distribution_variance.note: Seed distributions are ordinal with committee noise; advancement distributions nested.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and tournament games as the way the resume changes before Selection Sunday.

officiating_rules.note: Game officiating is not an input to selection; the relevant rules are the committee's principles and procedures, covered under protocol and settlement inputs.

settlement_contract.note: No series attached to this key has rules text; field size, play-in structure and bracketing rules for 2027 are unverified, so the contract mapping cannot be audited.

cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.label: Resume leverage of each remaining game (win and loss value by opponent quadrant and site)
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.mechanism: Each remaining game moves NET, quadrant records, WAB and SOR by amounts that depend on the opponent's rank and the site, so the final resume is a function of which games remain and who the team beats.
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.rationale: A bubble team's field probability depends more on whether its remaining games are Q1 opportunities (large upside, small downside) or Q4 traps (small upside, large downside) than on the average strength of remaining opponents.
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.measurement: For each remaining game g compute dWAB_win_g and dWAB_loss_g from the WAB formula using current opponent ranks and site; leverage_g = P(win_g) * dWAB_win + (1 - P(win_g)) * dWAB_loss; also compute dNET rank change by Monte Carlo (NET approximated by team value index and efficiency); aggregate final resume distribution by simulating all remaining games including conference tournament; as-of: current resume snapshot and schedule; recompute daily.
free_sources: NCAA NET rankings and team sheets (NCAA.com)
raw_data: opponent NET ranks and sites for remaining games
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.why: Replaces a remaining-strength-of-schedule average with the quadrant-based marginal value that the committee actually uses.

cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.label: Revealed committee weights on NET, WAB, SOR, quadrant record and predictive ratings by seed range
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.mechanism: The committee's ranking behaves like a latent score over the metrics with weights that differ at the top of the field and on the bubble.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.rationale: Using KenPom or NET alone ranks teams as an analyst would, not as the committee did; an ordered-probit fit on past seeds reveals that, for instance, quality wins count more at the top and bad losses more on the bubble.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.measurement: For seasons 2018 to 2026 (post-NET) fit an ordered probit for final seed (1 to 16, plus missed) on standardised NET rank, WAB, SOR, KPI, KenPom rank, Q1 wins, Q3+Q4 losses and conference tournament result, with weights allowed to vary in three seed bands (1-4, 5-10, 11-16 and bubble) via interaction terms; regularise with ridge; output coefficient vector with standard errors and the committee noise sd; as-of: metrics at Selection Sunday and weekly in March.
free_sources: NCAA.com NET archive and team sheets
raw_data: final seeds and field per year
metric values at Selection Sunday per team per year
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.why: Directly estimates the function the selection process applies and its noise, which no input in the existing list gives.

cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.label: Committee protocol vintage: metrics used, quadrant definitions, field size and bracketing rules
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.mechanism: The metrics on the team sheet, the quadrant thresholds, the number of bids and the bracketing rules change from year to year, shifting the relevant weights.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.rationale: Quadrant definitions and metric lists have been revised (for example the addition of WAB, adjustments to quadrant thresholds) and the field size may change for 2027 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); a model fit on earlier years can be mis-specified for the current protocol.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.measurement: Maintain a per-season record: metrics on team sheet, quadrant thresholds for home, neutral and away games, number of at-large and automatic bids, play-in structure, bracketing principle changes; indicator variables for protocol changes and a protocol-vintage weight for each historical season (1.0 for current protocol, 0.5 for one prior change, 0.25 for earlier) used in the fits; as-of: NCAA announcement dates.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.why: Makes the historical calibration data valid for the current year's rules.

cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.label: Committee weighting of recent results relative to the full season
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.mechanism: Committee members may weigh the last month of results and the conference tournament more heavily than early-season results, in contrast to metrics that weigh the season equally.
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.rationale: If recency is rewarded, late-season rises and falls move seed lines beyond what the cumulative metrics show; estimating it prevents using a static season-long metric when late results matter.
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.measurement: From the ordered-probit residuals (actual seed minus metric-implied seed) regress on last-10-games win share relative to season win share, last-10 efficiency margin minus season efficiency margin, and conference tournament games won, using 8 seasons; as-of: Selection Sunday; report coefficient with standard errors; use a prior of zero with a ridge shrinkage that corresponds to an sd of 0.5 seed lines per standard deviation of the recency variable.
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.why: Specific to the committee's process; without it the model assumes uniform time weights.

cbb.committee_availability_treatment.label: Seed adjustment for key players missing at Selection Sunday
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.mechanism: The committee takes player availability into account in some way, so a team missing a star may be placed lower (or protected) than metrics alone imply.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.rationale: An injury late in the season changes how good the team is without changing its resume; whether the committee seeds on full-strength or current-strength is a discrete, partially discretionary choice with a few lines at stake.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.measurement: From past years list teams with a rotation player (top 3 by minutes or BPM) out at Selection Sunday, compute seed residual from the revealed-preference model, estimate the mean residual by player importance (BPM share) with a prior mean of -0.5 lines and a sd of 1.0, shrinking by n/(n+10); as-of: injury status published before Selection Sunday.
raw_data: injury list at Selection Sunday per team per year
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.why: Gives a data-based seed shift for the availability category, absent from the existing list.

cbb.resume_metrics.reason: NET, quadrants, WAB and SOR are the team-sheet metrics the committee reads; correct primary but they must be projected forward to Selection Sunday, not read at today's values.

cbb.committee_seed_model.reason: Combines a model and a bracketologist consensus; the model part is a primary input, but the consensus is an expert benchmark and should be separated when evaluating edge.

cbb.ratings.reason: Predictive ratings are consulted by the committee but with less weight than results around the bubble; they are primary for round-reached outcomes after seeding.

cbb.bracket_sim.reason: Needed for advancement and seed placement; it is a method that integrates other inputs, and its field-size assumptions must be flagged.

cbb.conference_standings_sim.reason: Feeds the resume and the conference tournament seeding, but for national seed lines its impact is indirect.

cbb.auto_bid_structure.reason: Bid-thief count sets the at-large cutoff; the single largest structural driver of bubble probabilities.

cbb.conf_strength.reason: Conference strength affects non-conference strength-of-schedule and perceived quality; its size is moderate and partly inside NET.

cbb.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining strength of schedule is a crude average; the quadrant-based leverage input is the specific form the resume needs.

cbb.title_path.reason: Path strength after seeding is an output of the bracket simulation conditional on the draw, not an independent input.

cbb.seed_upset_priors.reason: Historical advancement by seed is a calibration target and a prior, but seeds already carry rating information, so it double counts if added to ratings.

cbb.news.reason: The label (coaching, award, ranking-poll news) does not match the stated use (selection and committee communications); the useful content is the committee's interim top-16 reveal and chair statements.

interactions.mechanism: For teams contending for a one or two seed, predictive ratings and quality wins dominate the committee's ordering, whereas on the bubble the quadrant record and bad losses dominate; the coefficient on predictive ratings relative to resume metrics therefore changes across seed bands.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the ordered probit with interaction terms by seed band and compare out-of-sample log-likelihood to a single-weight model.

interactions.mechanism: The number of bid thieves depends on the joint outcomes of 30 conference tournaments, so the distribution of at-large slots available to the bubble is a function of the sum of Bernoulli events with unequal probabilities; a single multi-bid league tournament upset can create a thief at once and change the cutoff for all bubble teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate all conference tournaments and compute the distribution of thieves and the bubble cutoff; compare to historical thief counts (0 to 4 per year).

interactions.mechanism: If the committee weights recent results more, the same cumulative metrics yield different seeds for teams that peaked early versus those that finished strong; the seed distribution is therefore conditional on trajectory in the last month.
interactions.how_to_test: Group teams with equal metric-implied seeds by last-10 trajectory and compare mean seed residuals.

interactions.mechanism: A bubble team's field probability is near zero or one unless its resume sits within a narrow band around the cutoff; games matter a lot only when the resume is in that band, so the leverage of a game is large near the cutoff and small for locks and for teams far outside.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the change in field probability from a Q1 win versus a Q3 loss for teams at different distances from the cutoff and verify a narrow high-leverage band.

interactions.mechanism: The seed shift for a missing star depends on how much of the team's rating the player carries; for a team whose value is spread across a deep roster the committee has little reason to move it, while for a one-star team the shift may be larger and uncertain in sign.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress seed residual on the missing player's share of team BPM for teams with a late injury across seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating in quality wins (Q1 count) and convex penalty for Q3 and Q4 losses
nonlinearities.why: Additional top-tier wins beyond about six add little to seed, while each additional bad loss costs more than the previous one, so the mapping from record to committee score is neither linear nor symmetric.

nonlinearities.shape: step: each extra bid thief moves the at-large cutoff by exactly one slot
nonlinearities.why: The effective number of at-large slots is an integer function of the thief count, so P(make field) for a bubble team jumps in discrete increments across the thief distribution rather than varying smoothly.

nonlinearities.shape: ordinal step function with fuzzy edges: P(seed line) is bell-shaped in rank with sd 2 to 4 slots
nonlinearities.why: A team ranked 4th or 5th overall has comparable probabilities of being a 1 seed or a 2 seed because of S-curve adjustments; the probability changes sharply across the line boundary rather than linearly with rating.
